unit1_text: Fundamentals of Quantum Mechanics Inadequacy of classical mechanics, de-Broglie concept of matter waves, Davisson and Germer experiment, wave packet, phase velocity, group velocity, Heisenberg’s uncertainty principle and its applications, time-dependent and time-independent Schrodinger wave equations, particle confined in one dimensional box, wave function and its physical interpretation.
unit2_text: Structure and properties of materials Atomic structure, types of bonding (ionic, covalent, metallic), crystal structures (BCC, FCC, HCP), lattice parameters, stress and strain, elastic modulus (Young's, Bulk, Shear).
unit3_text: Thermal Physics Laws of thermodynamics, heat conduction, convection and radiation, heat capacity, thermal expansion, thermal conductivity, melting and solidification, thermal resistance, enthalpy and entropy, equations of state, Newton's law of cooling.
unit4_text: Electrical and Magnetic Properties Band theory of solids, conductors, semiconductors, insulators, dielectric materials, piezoelectricity, ferro-electricity, magnetic materials (diamagnetic, paramagnetic, ferromagnetic), Hall effect, carrier concentration.
unit5_text: Photonics Fiber optics: Fundamental idea about optical fiber, acceptance angle, acceptance cone, numerical aperture, principle of light propagation in optical fiber, attenuation and attenuation coefficient in fibre. Laser: Interaction of radiation with matter (absorption, spontaneous and stimulated emission), principle of laser operation, Einstein’s coefficients, Ruby laser, He-Ne laser, laser applications.

unit1_text: Chemistry of Metals and Alloys: Electronic structure and metallic bonding, properties of engineering metals (iron, aluminium, copper, titanium), alloy formation and phase diagrams, heat treatment chemistry, hardening mechanisms (solid solution, precipitation, work hardening), non-destructive testing (NDT) chemical principles
unit2_text: Corrosion and Protection: Electrochemical theory of corrosion, types of corrosion (galvanic, pitting, crevice, intergranular, erosion-corrosion), corrosion in high-temperature environments, oxidation kinetics, passivation, cathodic and anodic protection, corrosion inhibitors, organic and inorganic coatings, galvanizing and electroplating

Analysis of Coal: Proximate, Ultimate analysis and their significance, Octane and Cetane numbers, biofuels (biodiesel, bioethanol), Biogas manufacturing
unit4_text: Sustainable Energy Chemistry: Electrochemical cells and EMF, galvanic and concentration cells, Nernst equation, fuel cells (H2-O2, PEM, SOFC), Li-ion and solid-state batteries, supercapacitors, hydrogen production (electrolysis, steam reforming), photovoltaic chemistry, thermochemical energy storage
unit5_text: Surface Engineering and Advanced Materials: Surface energy and wettability, physical and chemical vapor deposition (PVD/CVD), thermal spraying, ceramic coatings, diamond-like carbon (DLC) coatings, Nanomaterials: Properties of Nanomatrials, Applications of nanomaterials, Synthesis methods: Sol-gel and chemical vapour deposition, Carbon nanotubes.

unit1_text: Introduction: Classification of machine tools based on application and production rate: General purpose and Special purpose machines, Classification based on-types of machine tools and the processes. Dynamometer. Economics of metal cutting.
unit2_text: Lathe: Various types of lathe: Centre lathe, facing lathe, gap-bed lathe, capstan and turret lathe, NC, CNC and DNC lathe, major difference between CNC lathe and conventional lathe. unit3_text: Lathe Contd..: Driving mechanisms, apron mechanism, thread cutting mechanism and calculations, features of half-nut engagement – disengagement, indexing dial mechanism. Operations on lathe: taper turning, related calculations, thread cutting, facing, under-cutting, drilling, boring, parting-off, knurling, chamfering. Reciprocating Type Machine Tools: Shaper, Planer and Slotter: Constructional features, basic machines and kinematics and related calculations.
unit4_text: Drilling Machines: Constructional features of bench drilling machine, radial drilling machine, multi-spindle drilling machine, feed mechanism, work holding devices, Tool – holding devices. Different drilling operations: Drilling, reaming, counter boring and countersinking etc. estimation of drilling time. Milling Machines: Types of general purpose milling machines: horizontal, vertical, universal and their principal parts. Types of milling cutters and their applications, different milling operations, work-holding devices: vice, clamps, chucks, dividing head and its use, simple, compound and differential indexing. Indexing calculations and machining time calculations. Introduction to machining centers.
unit5_text: Grinding Machines: Different types of grinding machines: cylindrical, surface and centre-less grinding machines, basic constructional features and mechanisms, specifications, different grinding operations, honing, lapping and super-finishing processes. unit1_text: Single phase Transformer: Efficiency Voltage regulation, O.C.& S.C. Tests. Three Phase Transformer: Three phase transformer connections, 3-phase to 2-phase or 6-phase connections and their applications. Auto Transformer: Volt- Amp relations, efficiency, advantages & disadvantages, applications. D.C. Motors: Concept of starting, speed control, losses and efficiency.
unit2_text: Three phase Induction Motor: Construction, equivalent circuit, torque equation and torque- slip characteristics, speed control. Alternator: Construction, e.m.f. equation, Voltage regulation and its determination by synchronous impedance method. Control System: Open loop & closed loop controls, servo mechanisms; concept of various types of system. Signals: Unit step, unit ramp, unit impulse and periodic signals with their mathematical representation and characteristics.
unit4_text: Time Response Analysis: Time response of a standard second order system and response specifications, steady state errors and error constants. Stability: Concept and types of stability, Routh Hurwitz Criterion and its application for determination of stability, limitations; Polar plot, Nyquist stability Criterion and assessment of stability.
unit5_text: Root Locus Techniques: Concept of root locus, construction of root loci. Frequency Response Analysis: Correlation between time and frequency responses of a second order system; Bode plot, gain margin and phase margin and their determination from Bode and Polar plots. Process control: Introduction to P, PI and PID controllers their characteristics, representation and applications.

co1_text: Understand the main components of the hydraulic and pneumatic systems and their functions and symbols.
co2_text: Understand the advantages and disadvantages of hydraulic/pneumatic systems, and be aware of the underlying principles.
co3_text: Describe the construction, operation principles, and uses of auxiliary equipment, such as filters, oil coolers, oil heater and accumulators.

unit2_text: FLUID POWER ELEMENTS Pressure control valves, flow control valves, directional control valves – working principle and construction, special type valves, servo valves, Cartridge valves Actuation methods, Shock absorbers – Accumulator – Symbol for fluid power elements.
unit3_text: HYDRAULICS CIRCUITS Hydraulics circuits – automatic reciprocating circuit – speed control circuit - Meter in - Meter out – Sequencing Circuits – Synchronizing circuits, Accumulator circuit – Safety circuits – Hydraulic Motor braking System. Design of Hydraulic circuits
unit4_text: PNEUMATIC SYSTEMS Pneumatic fundamentals Filter, regulator, lubricator, air motors, air cylinders, pneumatic valves, Basic Pneumatic circuits – Hydro Pneumatic Systems – air- oil cylinder, air – oil reservoir, air – oil intensifier and simple circuits
unit5_text: FLUID LOGIC CONTROL Principle of fluid Logic control, Basic fluidic devices – Fluid sensors Fluidic circuits – sequencing control, continuous reciprocation, Electrical controls – electrical components – simple electro hydraulic/ pneumatic circuits. PLC application in fluid power control.

unit1_text:
PHYSICAL MODELING                                                                               8 
 
Concept of system and environment, continuous and discrete system, linear and 
nonlinear system, stochastic activities, static and dynamic models, principles used in 
modeling, Basic simulation modeling, Role of simulation in model evaluation and studies, 
Advantages and Disadvantages of simulation. Modeling of systems, Iconic, analog & 
Mathematical Modeling.
unit2_text:
COMPUTER BASED SYSTM SIMULATION 

Technique of simulation, Monte Carlo method, experimental nature of simulation, 
numerical computation techniques, calumnious system models, analog and hybrid 
simulation, feedback systems, Buildings simulation models of waiting line system, Job 
shop material handling and flexible manufacturing system.
unit3_text:
PROBABILITY CONCEPTS IN SIMULATION 

Stochastic variables, discrete and continuous probability functions, random 
numbers, generation of random numbers, variance reduction techniques, Determination 
of the length of simulation runs, Output analysis.
unit4_text:
SYSTEM DYNAMICS MODELING 

Identification of problem situation, preparation of causal loop diagrams and flow 
diagrams, equation writing, level and rate relationship, Simulation of system dynamics 
model.
unit5_text:
VERIFICATION AND VALIDATION 

Design of simulation experiments, validation of experimental models, testing and 
analysis. Simulation languages comparison and selection, study of SIMULA, DYNAMO, 
STELLA, POWERSIM. simulation software.

unit1_text: Mould production - equipment for moulding, moulding technique - pattern utilisation, hand and machine compaction, machine moulding, mould drying and hardening. Cores and core making - core boxes, compaction, core hardening, closing of moulds.
unit2_text: Melting Practice : Classification of melting furnaces, brief description of construction and operation of various furnaces - cupola and its design, electric arc furnaces, electric induction furnaces. Melting charge, melting conditions, melting losses, special melt treatment, melt quality control and recent development in metal melting.Pouring : Metal temperature, pouring equipment and techniques.
unit3_text: Shell moulding - Basic operation, production systems, characteristics of shell moulded casting and D-process. Investment Casting - expandable pattern process. Pattern production, investment, pattern removal and firing, casting.Factor influencing casting quality characteristics of precision investment casting.Investment casting from permanent casting.Die-casting - Gravity die-casting, pressure-die casting, die-casting machines, casting techniques, characteristics of die - castings.Centrifugal casting - Fundamental principles, methods production techniques, characteristics of centrifugal casting.
unit4_text: Crystallization and development of cast structure - Nucleation, Growth and dendrite growth, independent nucleation, eutectic freezing, paratactic relations, structure of castings - significance and practical control cast structure, grain shape and orientation, grain size, refinement and modification of cast structure. Concept of progressive and directional solidification, solidification time and derivation of Chvorinov’s equation influence of mould characteristics and cast metal. Properties on solidification, process numerical methods for heat flow analysis.
unit5_text: Feeding characteristics of alloys, geometric influences on solidification.Methods of the feeding of castings - cost and concept of yield, orientations, gating technique, casting temperature and pouring speed, design and location of feeder heads.Aids to feeder head efficiency, junction of feeder head and casting, use of padding, chills and insulators.

unit1_text: INTRODUCTION: History, Classification, comparison between conventional and non-conventional machining process selection. MECHANICAL PROCESS: Ultrasonic machining(USM): Introduction, Equipment, tool materials & tool Size, Abrasive slurry, Cutting tool system design:- Magnetostriction assembly, Tool cone(Concentrator), Exponential concentrator of circular cross section & rectangular cross section, Hallow cylindrical concentrator. Mechanics of cutting:-Theory of Miller & Shaw., Effect of parameter:-Effect of amplitude and frequency and vibration, Effect of grain diameter, Effect of applied static load, Effect of slurry, Tool & work material., USM process Characteristics:- Material removal rate, tool wear, Accuracy, surface finish., Applications, Advantages & Disadvantages of USM
unit2_text: ABRASIVE JET MACHINING(AJM): Introduction, Equipment, Variables in AJM:- Carrier Gas, Type of abrasive, Size of abrasive grain, velocity of the abrasive jet, Mean No. abrasive particles per unit volume of the carrier gas, Work meterial, stand off distance(SOD), nozzle design, Shape of cut. Process characteristics-Material removal rate, Nozzle wear, Accuracy & surface finish. Applications, Advantages & Disadvantages of AJM. ELECTORCHEMICAL AND CHEMICAL METAL REMOVAL PROCESS:- Electrochemical machining(ECM): Introduction, Study of ECM machine, Elements of ECM process:-Cathode tool, Anode work piece, source of DC power, Electrolyte. Chemistry of the process, ECM process characteristics-Material removal rate, Accuracy, Surface finish., ECM Tooling:-ECM tooling technique & example, Tool & insulation materials, Tool size Electrolyte flow arrangement, Handling of slug., Economics of ECM, Applications such as Electrochemical turning, Electrochemical Grinding, Electrochemical Honing, deburring, Advantages, Limitations.
unit3_text: CHEMICAL MACHINING(CHM): Introduction, Elements of process, Chemical blanking Process:-Preparation of workpiece, preparation of masters, masking with photo resists, etching for blanking, Accuracy of chemical blanking, Applications of chemical blanking, chemical milling(Contour machining):- Process steps-masking, Etching, process characteristics of CHM:- material removal rate accuracy, surface finish, Hydrogen embrittlement, Advantages & application of CHM. THERMAL METAL REMOVAL PROCESSES: Electrical discharge machining(EDM)-introduction, machine, mechanism of metal removal, dielectric fluid, spark generator, EDM tools(electrodes) Electrode feed control, Electrode manufacture, Electrode wear, EDM tool design: Choice of machining operation, electrode material selection, under sizing and length of electrode, Machining time. Flushing-Pressure flushing, suction flushing, side flushing, pulsed flushing synchronized with electrode movement, EDM process characteristics: Metal removal rate, Accuracy surface finish, Heat affected Zone. Machine tool selection, Application: EDM accessories /applications, electrical discharge grinding, Travelling wire EDM.
unit4_text: PLASMA ARC MACHINING(PAM): Introduction, equipment non-thermal generation of plasma, selection of gas, Mechanism of Metal removal, PAM parameters, Process characteristics. Safety precautions, Applications, Advantages and limitations.
unit5_text: Derived and Hybrid Modern manufacturing Methods: Introduction of process like rotary ultrasonic machining , electro stream drilling, shape tube eletro machining,  wire electro discharge machining, electro chemical grinding, electro chemical honing, electro chemical deburring and electro chemical spark machining.

unit1_text:
INTRODUCTION TO GEARS 

Types of gears, classification, gear drawings, gearboxes, application of gears, gear production methods, an overview. 
GEAR MATERIALS  
Non-metallic, ferrous and non-ferrous gears. Properties of gear materials, selection of material for typical gears and applications – blank preparation methods for different gears, size, type and material.
unit2_text:
PRODUCTION OF GEARS & SCREW THREADS 

Gear milling different gears, cut quality obtainable. Gear hobbing, description and operation of machine, types of gears cut, hobbing cutters, work holding methods gear shaping, disc type and rack type gear shapers, Production of straight bevel gears and spiral gears, milling, generation by straight bevel gear generator. Duplex cutter, straight bevel gear generator, Spiral bevel gear generator. 
PRODUCTION OF SCREW THREADS:  Screw thread terminology, Types of screw thread, Methods of producing screw threads, Effect of pitch errors, measurement of various elements of screw threads. Thread rolling, Thread Grinding, Mass Production of Screws.
unit3_text:
HEAT TREATMENT OF GEARS 

Through hardening, case hardening, flames hardening, induction hardening of gears, Nitriding of gears. Tuft riding of gears. Inspection of gears for hardening defects 

GEAR FINISHING 

Gear finishing advantages, finishing of gears by grinding, shaving, lapping, honing methods and cold rolling of gears. Description of machines, process and process parameters
unit4_text:
GEAR INSPECTION 

Types of gear errors, gear quality standards tooth thickness and base tangent length measurement, pitch errors, radial run out errors, profile errors, pitch error measurement. Composite error measurement. Computerized gear inspection centers. Reasons and remedies for gear errors
unit5_text:
MODERN GEAR PRODUCTION METHODS 

Gear production by stamping, die casting, power metal process, injection and compression Moulding in plastics. Die casting, cold and hot rolling, mass production methods shear speed shaping. Gear broaching – Gleason. G-Trac Gear generation method

Computer Aided Metrology – Principles and interfacing, software metrology.

Laser metrology – Applications of Lasers in precision measurements – Laser 
interferometer, speckle measurements, Laser scanners. Introduction to Nano-
metrology.
unit2_text:
•

Non-contact sensors for surface finish measurements.
unit3_text:
Basic functional elements and classification of instruments. Basic concepts like 
sensitivity, threshold, resolution, precision and accuracy, linearity, zero drift, 
sensitivity drift, etc. Relation between concepts.
unit4_text:
Definition for source of error and methods of minimizing for eliminating the effects of 
error sources like friction, play, temperature, loading error, etc. Error and least count 
through four-quadrant diagram. 
Uncertainty of measurements, static calibration, Error in computed value and 
rounding -off procedure.
unit5_text:
Dynamic characteristics of zero- order, first-order, and second-order instruments 
for step, ramp, sinusoidal and impulse inputs. Signal conditioners like bridge 
circuit, amplifiers, and low pass filter and radio telemetry, Analysis of random 
signals. Measurement of quantities like displacement, velocity, acceleration, 
force, torque, temperature, pressure, vacuum, sound, flow, and level.

unit1_text:
Introduction:  

Concept and evoluation of quality control Measurement & Metrology, Precision vs accuracy. Process capability, standrdisation & Interchangeability. 


Inspection and Gauges:  

Inspection methods. Types of Gauges. Limits Fits and Tolerances. Non-Destructive Testings & Evaluation.
unit2_text: Control Charts for SQC: Statistical Quality Control (SQC). Control charts for variables such as X, R charts and control charts for attributes such as p-charts, c-chart. Construction & use of the control charts. Process capability.
unit3_text: Acceptance Sampling for SQC: Principle of acceptance sampling. Producer's and consumer's risk. Sampling plans - Single, double & sequential. Sampling by attributes and variables.
unit4_text:
Reliability:  

Introduction to reliability, bath-tub curve. Life expectancy. Reliability based design. Series & Parallel system.






Defect Diagnosis and prevention:  

Basic causes of failure, curve/control of failure. MTBF. Maintainability, Condition monitoring and diagnostic techniques.
Value Engineering: Elements of value analysis, Techniques.
unit5_text:
TQM: Inspection, Quality control, Quality Assurance and Quality Management and Total Quality Management. Implementation of TQM. ISO 9000 and its series, Zero defect. Quality circle. Taguchi Method.




Other Factors in Quality: Human Factors such as attitude and errors. Material-Quality. Machine Capability and Manufacturing process limitations. Quality in sales & service. Methods for improving accuracy & quality.

1.  Introduction : Objective & advantages of heat treatment of metals . 
           02 Hrs

04 Hrs
unit2_text:
3. Heat Treatment of Steel : Principles of heat treating of steels, quantitative prediction of transformation hardening in steels, stress-relief heat treating of steel, normalizing of steel, annealing of steel, continuous annealing of steel, quenching of steel, tempering of steel, mar tempering of steel, austempering of steel, induction heat treating of steel, cold treating and cryogenic treatment of steel,  heat treating of ultra high strength steels. Heat treating maraging steels, heat-treating of powder metallurgy steels, thermo mechanical processing of steels.  




10 Hrs
unit3_text:
4. Heat Treating Equipment : Types of heat treating furnaces salt bath equipment, fluidized-bed equipment, heat treating in vacccum furnaces and auxiliary equipment, heat resistant material for furnace parts trays and fixtures. Enery-efficient furnace design and operation - like batch type, box muffle, and salt bath furnace.  

08 Hrs
unit4_text:
5. Surface Hardening of Steel : Introduction of surface hardening of steels, flame hardening, laser surface hardening, electron beam surface hardening, gas carburizing, pack carburizing, liquid carburizing and cyaniding, vacuum, carburizing, plasma (Ion) nit riding, gaseous and plasma nitro carburizing, bronzing (Bronizing), thermo-reactive, deposition/diffusion process, methods of measuring case depth.


10 Hrs
unit5_text:
6. Process and Quality Control Considerations : Temperature control, furnace and atmospheres, furnace atmosphere control, control of surface carbon contents in heat treating of steel. Evaluation of carbon control in processed parts. Defects and distraction in heat-treated parts. Statistical process control of heat-treated parts, statistical process control heat-treating operations. Computerized properties prediction and technology planning in heat treatment of steel. Furnace Safety.  


08 Hrs

unit1_text:
1. JIT  - An Introduction : Spread of JIT movement, the new production system research association of Japan, some definitions of JIT, core Japanese practices of JIT, creating continuous manufacture, enabling JIT to occur, basic element of JIT, benefits of JIT.




02Hrs
2. Modern Production System : Key feature of Toyota’s production system, basic framework of Toyota production system. 
Kanban System : other types of kanban’s , kanban rules, adapting to fluctuations in demand through kanban, whirlging, determining the number of kanban’s in Toyota production system, detailed kanban system example, supplier kanban and the sequence schedule for use by suppliers.



04Hrs
unit2_text:
Production smoothing in Toyota production system - production planning, production smoothing, adaptability to demand fluctuations, sequencing method for the mixed model assembly line to realize smoothed production. Criticism to Toyota production system by the communist party of Japan. EDP system for support of the Toyota production system. Shortening lead time in Toyota production system - reducing the setup time. Automation in Toyota production system, some comparisons with other manufacturers.


8 Hrs 

3. Global Implementation of JIT : JIT in automotive industry, JIT in electronics, computer, telecommunication and instrumentation, JIT in process type industry, JIT in seasonal demand industry, other manufacturing industries, JIT in service and administrative operations, conclusion  


03Hrs
unit3_text:
4.  Design, Development and Management of JIT Manufacturing Systems : Plant  configurations and flow analysis for JIT manufacturing, comparison of JIT’s “demand pull” system with conventional “push type” planning and control systems, quality management system for JIT, product design for JIT human resource management in JIT, flexible workforce system at Toyota, creation and maintenance of teams of JIT, union organisation and conduct of industrial relations in JIT, interface of JIT with advanced manufacturing technology, assessing performance in JIT manufacturing systems, product costing information systems in JIT manufacturing, an example of overhead allocation in JIT, potential for developing countries, potential for small manufacturing.




10 Hrs
unit4_text:
5. Supply Management for JIT : JIT purchasing-the Japanese way, some studies in JIT purchasing, experience of implementation organisations, surveys on JIT purchasing, buyer-seller relationship in JIT purchasing, quality certification of suppliers in JIT purchasing, monitoring supplier performance for  JIT purchasing, audit in JIT purchasing, implementation of JIT to international sourcing, frequency of shipments, inventory policy, supplier reaction capability, quality, communication sole sourcing, delivery performance and supplier flexibility, conclusion. 


10 Hrs
unit5_text:
6. Framework for Implementation of JIT : Implementation risk, risks due to inappropriate understanding of JIT, risks due to technical, operational and people problems, risks associated with kanban system, some important activities to be performed during implementation, steps in implementation, a project work to approach to implementation, conclusion.  


05Hrs

unit1_text: Introduction Digital image representation; fundamental steps in image processing; elements of digital image processing systems: image acquisition, storage, processing and display. 2. Digital Image Fundamentals : Structure of the human eye; image formation; brightness adaptation and discrimination; a simple image model; uniform and non‐uniform sampling and quantization; some basic relationships between pixels; neighbors of a pixel; connectivity; Labeling. Distance measures; imaging geometry.
unit2_text: Image Enhancement in the spatial domain 4L Basic gray level transformations‐histogram processing‐Enhancement using arithmetic/logic operations‐Basics of spatial filtering‐comparison between smoothing and sharpening spatial filters.
unit3_text: Image Enhancement in the frequency domain 4L1D Fourier transform‐2D Fourier transform and its Inverse‐Smoothing & sharpening frequency domain filters (Ideal, Butterworth, Gaussian)‐homomorphic filtering. Image compression 4L Fundamentals‐Image compression, Error‐free compression: Huffman coding, block coding, constant area coding, variable length coding; bit‐plane coding; lossless predictive coding.
unit4_text: Machine Vision 12L Introduction, definition, human visual system. Active vision system, increasing of machine vision. Machine vision components, hardware’s and algorithms, image function and characteristics, image formation & image sensing frequency space analysis, Fourier transform, convolution algorithms, image gaussion, image enhancement, image analysis and segmentation data reduction, feature extraction, edge detection, image recognition and decisions, m/c learning, image processing, machine vision edges detection, application in the area such as inspection part identification, industrial robot control, mobile robot application. Industrial MVs in production and services, structure of industrial m/c vision, generic standards, rules of thumb, image formation, illumination, optics, interfacing machine vision system. Vision system calibration.
unit5_text: 2D&3D vision 6L 16 Competing technologies, principle, CCD, Videcon and other cameras, data capture. Triangulation geometry, resolution, passive and active 3‐D stereo imaging, data processing

university_name: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University, Lucknow
co1_text: Understand the manufacturing systems, flexibility, components of FMS
co2_text: Understand production, planning, scheduling and simulation of FMS
co3_text: Understand concepts of group technology and economics issues in the application of FMS
co4_text: Understand the application of FMS in various operations & involvement of AI in flexible manufacturing system.
co6_text: Apply the concepts of scheduling in FMS
co5_text: Understand the concepts of scheduling and simulation in FMS
unit1_text:
Understanding of FMS
Introduction To FMS, Evolution of Manufacturing Systems, objective and Need, Benefits, Components, Types of Flexibility, Merits, Demerits and Applications of Flexibility.
Composition of FMS, CNC machines, robots, automatic storage and retrieval, automatic material handling, computerized control, Hierarchy of Computer Control ,Computer Control of Work Centre and Assembly Lines, FMS Supervisory Computer Control.
unit2_text:
Planning, scheduling and control of flexible manufacturing systems:
Process planning, machine loading, cycle time, machine output vs cycle time, methods to reduce cycle time, machine balancing.
Scheduling, data requirement for scheduling, mater production scheduling, Gantt charts, scheduling rules, scheduling in FMS, Single Product, Single Batch, N–Batch Scheduling Problem, Knowledge Based Scheduling System.
Dispatching, Dispatch activities.
unit3_text:
FMS simulation and data base
Application of Simulation, Model of FMS, Simulation Software, Limitation, Manufacturing Data Systems, Data Flow, FMS Database Systems, Planning For FMS Database.
Introduction to factors affecting the Performance of FMS, Introduction to Analytical model and Simulation model of FMS.
unit4_text:
Group technology and justification of FMS
Introduction, Matrix Formulation, Mathematical Programming Formulation, Graph Formulation, Knowledge Based System for Group Technology, Economic Justification Of FMS, Implementation issues and maintenance of FMS, Application of Possibility Distributions in FMS Systems Justification.
unit5_text:
Applications of FMS and factory of the future
FMS Application in Machining, Sheet Metal Fabrication, Prismatic Component Production, Aerospace Application, FMS Development Towards Factories of The Future, Artificial Intelligence and Expert Systems in FMS, Design Philosophy and Characteristics for Future, case studies.

co1_text: Understand modern product development theories and customer needs.
co2_text: Understand product tears down methods and product modularity.
co3_text: Understand concepts of modelling and morphological analysis.
co4_text: Understand material properties and economic factors influencing design
co5_text: Understand the significance of value engineering.
unit1_text:
Product development verses design, modern product development theories and methodologist in design. Product development teams.Product development planning, technical and business concerns. Understanding customer needs, Establishing product functions. Functional decomposition, modeling process, Function trees system functionality, augmentation.

Aggregation, common basis, functional modeling methods
unit2_text:
Product tear down and experimentation, benchmarking and establishing engineering specification. Product portfolios and portfolio architecture.

Tear down process, tear down methods, post teardown reporting, benchmarking approach, support tools, setting specifications, portfolio architecture, types, platform, functional architecting, optimization selection. Product modularity, modular design.
unit3_text: Generation of concepts, information gathering and brain storming, directed search,morphological analysis, combining solutions. Decision making, estimation of technical feasibility, concept selection process, selection charts, measurement theory, numerical concept scoring, design evaluation scheme, concept embodiment, geometry and layout, system modeling, modeling of product metrics, selection of model by performance specifications, physical prototyping, informal and formal models.
unit4_text:
Material properties, metals, plastics, rubber, woods & factors considered while designing for metals, plastics, rubber, woods etc, Anthropometry factors, physiological factors, psychology factors, anatomy factors.
Economic factors influencing design, product value, safety, reliability & environmental considerations, economic analysis, break even analysis, profit & competitiveness, economics of a new product design.
unit5_text:
Introduction, historical perspective, nature & measurement of value, importance of value, value analysis job plan, creativity, steps for solving & value analysis, value analysis tests
Principal stress trajectories( force flow lines), balanced design, criteria & objective of design, material toughness, resilience, designing for uniform strength.

unit1_text: Artificial Muscles: After a general overview of artificial muscle technologies used in robotics, the students fabricate dielectric elastomer actuators (DEAs) by hand and test the mechanical and electrical properties of their devices, comparing their results with theoretical predictions.
unit2_text: Outdoor Flying Robots: This is a practical exercise on the design of a combined altitude and speed controller for a miniature autonomous airplane. unit3_text: Teaching Robots to Accomplish a Manipulation Task: In this robotic practical, the student will be teaching a robot to build a tower by stacking several objects on top of each other. Industrial Robot Control: The goal is to control a robot specifically designed for tasks such as assembly, manipulation or packaging where there is need of fast and precise actions.
unit4_text: Haptics: After a brief overview of the state of the art of haptic devices, the students need to generate useful sensations in respect to a give problem, study the type of sensations that can be produced, as well as how they can be programmed. Assembly, programming and characterization of a modular fish robot: This practical is aimed at realizing a swimming fish robot using the same modules used for the Salamandra robotica II and AmphiBot III robots.

unit1_text: Overview: Intelligent / Smart materials – Functional materials – Polyfunctional materials – Structural materials, Electrical materials, bio-compatible materials. – Intelligent biological materials – Biomimetics – Wolff’s Law – Biocompatibility. Material response: swelling and leaching, corrosion and dissolution, deformation and failure, friction and wear – host response: the inflammatory process – coagulation and hemolysis – in vitro and in vivo evaluation of biomaterials.
unit2_text: Electro-Rheological & piezoelectric materials: The principal ingredients of smart materials –microsensors- hybrid smart materials - an algorithm for synthesizing smart materials – active, passive reactive actuator based smart structures- suspensions and electro-rheological fluids. Bingham body model – principal characteristics of electro-rheological fluids – charge migration mechanism for the dispersed phase – electro- rheological fluid domain – fluid actuators- design parameter – application of Electo-rheological fluids. Basics, Principles and instrumentation and application of Magnetorheological fluids – Piezoelectric materials: polymers and ceramics, mechanism, properties and application. Introduction to electro-restrictive and magneto-restrictive materials.
unit3_text: Shape memory materials: Nickel – Titanium alloy (Nitinol) – Materials characteristics of Nitinol – martensitic transformations – austenitic transformations – thermoelastic martensitic transformations. Classification of SMA alloys- mechanism of magnetic SMA – applications of SMA – continuum applications of SMA fasteners – SMA fibers – reaction vessels, nuclear reactors, chemical plant, etc. – micro robot actuated by SMA. SMA memorization process (Satellite Antenna Applications) SMA blood clot filter – Impediments to applications of SMA – Shape memory polymers– mechanism of shape memory-Primary moulding – secondary moulding– types and applications.
unit4_text: Orthopaedic and dental materials: Bone and teeth composition, formation and properties – bioresorbable, bioinert, bioactive materials - temporary fixation devices – joint replacement. Biomaterials used in bone and joint replacement metals and alloys- Fillings and restoration materials – Materials for oral and maxillofacial surgery – dental cements and dental amalgams – dental adhesives- bone tissue engineering.
unit5_text: Applications of materials: Blood clotting – blood theology– approaches to thrombo resistance materials development– blood vessels – The heart – aorta and valves – geometry of blood circulation – cardiac pacemakers – blood substitutes – extracorporeal blood circulation devices. The lungs – vascular implants: vascular graft, cardiac valve prostheses, card– Biomaterials in opthalmology –skin grafts -connective tissue grafts – tissue adhesives – drug delivery methods and materials.

unit1_text: UNIT 1: INTRODUCTION TO MINE ENVIRONMENT AND POLLUTION SOURCES Introduction to Mine Environmental Engineering: Definition, scope, and interdisciplinary nature. Sources and Types of Mine Pollution: Air Pollution: Dust (particulate matter PM10, PM2.5), gaseous emissions (NOx, SOx, CO, CH4), noise, vibrations. Water Pollution: Acid Mine Drainage (AMD), heavy metals, suspended solids, dissolved solids, process chemicals, oil and grease. Land Pollution: Overburden, waste rock, tailings, hazardous waste, soil degradation, land subsidence. Biodiversity Impacts: Habitat destruction, fragmentation, loss of flora and fauna, invasive species. Environmental Impacts of Mining: Impact on air quality, human health, and climate. Impact on surface water and groundwater quality and quantity. Impact on soil fertility, land stability, and landscape aesthetics. Impact on ecosystems, biodiversity, and ecosystem services. Basic Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) in Mining: Purpose and components of EIA for mining projects. Baseline data collection and impact prediction (conceptual overview).
unit2_text: UNIT-2: MINE WATER MANAGEMENT AND TREATMENT Mine Hydrology and Hydrogeology: Impact of mining on surface and groundwater regimes. Water balance in mining areas. Dewatering techniques for open-pit and underground mines. Water conservation strategies: Rainwater harvesting, water recycling and reuse. Acid Mine Drainage (AMD) Management: AMD Formation: Pyrite oxidation, role of bacteria, chemical reactions. Prediction of AMD: Static and Kinetic tests (conceptual). AMD Prevention Techniques: Encapsulation of reactive wastes, dry covers, anoxic limestone drains (ALD), passive reactive barriers. Mine Water Treatment Technologies: Active Treatment: Neutralization (lime, caustic soda), precipitation of heavy metals, coagulation-flocculation, sedimentation. Passive Treatment: Constructed wetlands, anoxic limestone drains, successive alkalinity producing systems (SAPS), bioreactors. Advanced Treatment: Membrane filtration (RO, UF), ion exchange, adsorption (conceptual). Tailings Dam Safety and Management: Types of tailings dams and their construction. Causes of tailings dam failures (liquefaction, overtopping, foundation failure). Design considerations for stability and environmental protection. Monitoring and surveillance of tailings storage facilities.
unit3_text: UNIT 3: MINE AIR QUALITY, VENTILATION, AND NOISE CONTROL Mine Air Pollutants and Health Impacts: Dust: Types (respirable, inhalable), sources (drilling, blasting, crushing, haulage), health effects (pneumoconiosis). Gases: Methane (CH4), Carbon Monoxide (CO), Carbon Dioxide (CO2), NOx, SOx, Hydrogen Sulphide (H2S). Sources of gases: Blasting, diesel engines, spontaneous combustion, strata gases. Physiological effects of mine gases. Mine Ventilation Principles: Objectives of mine ventilation: Dilution of pollutants, temperature control, provision of fresh air. Dust Control Measures: Prevention: Wet drilling, water infusion, proper blasting techniques. Suppression: Water spraying, chemical suppressants, dust collectors (wet scrubbers, bag filters). Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Respirators. Dust sampling and monitoring. Mine Gas Control and Fire Management: Gas Drainage: Methane drainage systems. Dilution and Removal: Ventilation strategies. Spontaneous Combustion: Causes, detection, and prevention methods (sealing, inertization). Mine Fires: Types, causes, detection, and suppression techniques. Noise and Vibration Control: Sources of noise and vibration in mining (machinery, blasting). Health impacts of noise. Noise abatement measures: Enclosures, silencers, anti-vibration mounts, operational controls. Vibration monitoring and control.
unit4_text: UNIT 4: MINE WASTE MANAGEMENT AND LAND RECLAMATION Mine Solid Waste Characterization and Management: Overburden and Waste Rock: Geochemical characterization, volume estimation, disposal strategies. Tailings: Physical and chemical properties, dewatering, disposal methods (dry stacking, paste fill, filtered tailings). Other Wastes: Hazardous waste (e.g., used oil, chemicals), scrap metal, domestic waste. Principles of waste minimization and resource recovery from mine waste. Design of Waste Dumps and Tailings Storage Facilities: Geotechnical stability analysis of dumps and impoundments. Drainage design for dumps and tailings facilities. Progressive backfilling and co-disposal techniques. Environmental considerations in design (e.g., leachate collection, liner systems). Mine Land Reclamation and Rehabilitation: Principles of Reclamation: Restoring land to a stable, non-polluting, and productive state. Topsoil Management: Stripping, stockpiling, and replacement. Landform Design: Creating stable and aesthetically pleasing landforms. Soil Amelioration: Improving soil fertility and structure (e.g., liming, organic matter addition). Revegetation Techniques: Selection of appropriate plant species (native, fast-growing, nitrogen-fixing). Seeding methods: Direct seeding, hydroseeding. Planting techniques: Seedlings, saplings. Monitoring of vegetation establishment and success. Post-Mining Land Use and Biodiversity Restoration: Planning for diverse and sustainable post-mining land uses (e.g., agriculture, forestry, recreation, conservation). Restoration of natural drainage patterns and water bodies. Strategies for re-establishing ecological connectivity and wildlife habitats. Long-term monitoring and maintenance of rehabilitated sites.
unit5_text: UNIT 5: ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS, REGULATIONS, AND SUSTAINABLE MINING Environmental Management Systems (EMS) in Mining: Introduction to ISO 14001 and its application. Elements of EMS: Environmental policy, planning, implementation, checking, and management review. Environmental performance indicators and reporting. Indian Environmental Laws and Regulations for Mining: Environmental (Protection) Act, 1986, and associated rules (e.g., Hazardous Waste Management Rules). Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981. Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, and Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. Mines Act, 1952, and relevant regulations (e.g., Coal Mines Regulations, Metalliferous Mines Regulations) related to environmental safety. Environmental Clearance process for mining projects (revisited). Environmental Monitoring and Auditing: Purpose and types of environmental monitoring (compliance, impact, baseline). Environmental auditing: Objectives, types, and methodology. Role of regulatory bodies in monitoring and enforcement. Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Sustainable Mining: Ethical considerations and social license to operate. CSR initiatives in the Indian mining sector. Community engagement, benefit sharing, and grievance redressal mechanisms. Principles of responsible mining and global initiatives (e.g., ICMM, TSM). Emerging Trends and Challenges: Climate change impacts on mining (e.g., water stress, extreme weather). Digitalization and automation for environmental management (IoT, AI, remote sensing). Circular economy principles in mining (resource recovery from waste). Deep-sea mining and its environmental implications. Challenges in managing legacy mine sites.

co1_text: Students will understand the fundamental concepts and principles underlying both physical and numerical simulation techniques.
co2_text: Students will be able to apply dimensional analysis and understand the methodology and material selection for physical modelling in engineering problems.
co3_text: Students will gain proficiency in the theoretical foundations and application of the Boundary Element Method (BEM), including specific techniques like the displacement-discontinuity method.
co4_text: Students will comprehend the Finite Difference Method (FDM) and its mesh generation, along with the ability to identify and apply both FDM and Finite Element Method (FEM) to solve relevant mining-related problems.
unit1_text: UNIT-1 Introduction to Simulation and Physical Modeling Fundamentals: Introduction to Simulation: Definition and purpose of simulation in engineering and science, Role of modelling, Classification of simulation types: Physical vs. Numerical, Deterministic vs. Stochastic, Static vs. Dynamic, Overview of the simulation process: Problem definition, model formulation, Fundamentals of Physical Modeling: Concept of physical models and their applications, Dimensional Analysis: Dimensions and units, homogeneity of equations, Buckingham Pi Theorem and its application, Similitude and Model Laws: Geometric, Kinematic, and Dynamic Similitude, Scaling laws for various physical phenomena (fluid flow, heat transfer, structural mechanics), Distorted models and their implications.
unit2_text: UNIT-2 Experimental Design and Data Analysis in Physical Simulation: Experimental Design for Physical Models: Planning and execution of physical experiments, Selection of model scales and materials, Measurement Techniques and Instrumentation: Sensors for measuring physical quantities, Data acquisition systems (DAS) and signal conditioning, Calibration of instruments and measurement accuracy, non-intrusive measurement techniques , Data Analysis and Interpretation: Statistical analysis of experimental data, Error analysis and uncertainty quantification, Regression analysis and curve fitting, Visualization of experimental results, Comparison of model results with prototype behavior.
unit3_text: UNIT- 3 Fundamentals of Numerical Simulation: Mathematical Modeling and Discretization: Mathematical Modeling of Physical Systems: Conservation laws: Mass, Momentum, Energy, Derivation of governing partial differential equations (PDEs) for: Heat Conduction (Diffusion Equation), Fluid Flow (Navier-Stokes Equations, Continuity Equation), Solid Mechanics (Stress-Strain relations, Equilibrium Equations), Introduction to Numerical Methods: Concept of discretization: Transforming continuous problems into discrete algebraic equations, Finite Difference Method (FDM): Taylor series expansion for approximating derivatives, Forward, Backward, and Central difference schemes, Finite Element Method (FEM): Concept of elements and nodes, Shape functions and interpolation, Weak formulation and weighted residual methods (Galerkin method), Application to 1D bar and heat transfer problems.
unit4_text: UNIT- 4 Advanced Numerical Simulation Techniques and Applications: Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD): Navier-Stokes equations and their challenges, Discretization of convective and diffusive terms, Pressure-velocity coupling algorithms (e.g., SIMPLE, PISO), Turbulence modeling (RANS, LES, DNS - conceptual overview), Grid generation and meshing strategies, Applications: Aerodynamics, hydrodynamics, heat exchangers, combustion, Finite Element Analysis (FEA): Review of FEM for 2D problems (plane stress/strain, axisymmetric problems), Discrete Element Method (DEM) for granular materials, Molecular Dynamics (MD) for atomic/molecular level simulations, Boundary Element Method (BEM), Meshless methods, Introduction to Commercial Simulation Software: Overview of popular software packages (e.g., ANSYS, ABAQUS, COMSOL, Open FOAM).
unit5_text: UNIT -5 Validation, Verification, and Advanced Topics: Verification and Validation (V&V) of Simulations: Verification: Ensuring the numerical model correctly solves the mathematical model, Validation: Ensuring the mathematical model accurately represents the real physical system (comparison with experimental data, analytical solutions), Uncertainty quantification in simulation. subject_name: Environmental Hazards and Disaster Management in Mines
subject_name_print: ENVIRONMENTAL HAZARDS AND DISASTER MANAGEMENT IN MINES
university_name: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University, Lucknow
co1_text: Students will be able to identify the causes and mechanisms of common mining hazards such as mine fires, explosions, and inundations, and apply appropriate preventive and control measures.
co2_text: Students will gain comprehensive knowledge of various mine occupational diseases, understanding their causes, symptoms, and the necessary preventive strategies for worker health.
co3_text: Students will develop the ability to plan and implement effective disaster management strategies in mines, including emergency organization, rescue operations, and the use of specialized equipment.
co4_text: Students will understand the legal and procedural requirements for disaster investigation and mine rescue rules, enabling them to contribute to a safer mining environment.
unit1_text: UNIT- 1: Introduction to Environmental Hazards in Mining: Fundamentals of Environmental Hazards and Disasters, Geological and Geotechnical Hazards: Slope Instability, Seismicity, Groundwater Issues, Soil Erosion and Sedimentation, Hydrological and Hydrogeological Hazards: Acid Mine Drainage (AMD): Formation mechanisms, prediction, and impacts on water bodies. Tailings Dam Failures: Causes (e.g., liquefaction, overtopping), impacts of spills. Mine Flooding: In open-pit and underground mines, impacts on operations and environment. Water Contamination: Heavy metals, dissolved solids, process chemicals. Atmospheric and Air Quality Hazards: Dust Emissions, Gaseous Emissions: NOx, SOx, CO from machinery and blasting. Spontaneous Combustion of Coal: Hazards, detection, and control. Biological and Ecological Hazards: Habitat Loss and Fragmentation: Impact on biodiversity. Invasive Species: Introduction through mining activities. Contamination of Food Chains: Bioaccumulation of heavy metals.
unit2_text: UNIT- 2: Risk Assessment and Monitoring of Environmental Hazards in Mines: Environmental Risk Assessment Methodology: Hazard identification, consequence analysis, likelihood assessment, Quantitative and qualitative risk assessment approaches. Integration of environmental risk assessment into mine planning, Geotechnical and Hydrological Monitoring: Slope Stability Monitoring: Geodetic surveys (GPS, Total Station), inclinometers, extensometers, radar, Groundwater Monitoring: Piezometers, monitoring wells, flow meters, Surface Water Monitoring: Flow gauges, water quality sensors (pH, EC, heavy metals). Tailings Dam Monitoring: Piezometers, settlement markers, visual inspections. Air Quality and Dust Monitoring: Ambient air quality monitoring stations (PM, SO2, NO2). Personal dust samplers. Noise level monitoring. Meteorological data collection for dispersion modeling. Ecological and Biodiversity Monitoring: Baseline ecological surveys. Monitoring of flora and fauna populations. Bio-indicators for environmental health. Data Management and Analysis for Monitoring: Use of GIS for spatial data management and visualization of monitoring results. Statistical analysis of environmental data. Reporting and communication of monitoring outcomes.
unit3_text: UNIT- 3: Disaster Management Principles and Frameworks: Disaster Management Cycle: Prevention/Mitigation: Long-term measures to reduce risk, Preparedness: Planning and readiness for response, Response: Actions during and immediately after a disaster. Recovery/Rehabilitation: Long-term restoration, Institutional Framework for Disaster Management in India: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA). State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs). District Disaster Management Authorities (DDMAs). Role of Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Mines, DGMS. Legal Framework for Disaster Management: Disaster Management Act, 2005. Relevant provisions in Mines Act, 1952; Mines Rules, 1955; Coal Mines Regulations, 2017; Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 (with focus on safety and environmental aspects). Environmental (Protection) Act, 1986, and rules related to hazardous waste management Types of Disaster Management Plans: National Disaster Management Plan. State and District Disaster Management Plans. On-site and Off-site Emergency Plans for Mines. Crisis Management Plans, Coordination and Communication.
unit4_text: UNIT- 4: Mitigation and Preparedness for Mining Disasters: Mitigation of Geotechnical Hazards: Slope Stability Measures, Subsidence Control, Seismic Hazard Mitigation: Blasting design, monitoring. Mitigation of Hydrological Hazards: AMD Prevention, Tailings Dam Safety, Mine Water Management, Mitigation of Air Quality Hazards: Dust Control, Ventilation Systems, Fire Prevention, Emergency Preparedness in Mines: Emergency Response Plans (ERP), Mock Drills and Training, Emergency Equipment and Infrastructure: Rescue teams, medical facilities, communication systems, Early Warning Systems, Role of Technology in Preparedness: Remote sensing and GIS for hazard mapping and vulnerability assessment, Real-time monitoring systems and automated alarms, Predictive modeling for environmental phenomena (e.g., AMD plume dispersion).
unit5_text: UNIT-5: Emergency Response, Rehabilitation, and Policy Framework: Emergency Response Operations, Post-Disaster Recovery and Rehabilitation: Short-term recovery measures, Long-term environmental rehabilitation: Landform reconstruction, soil amelioration, revegetation, water body restoration, Socio-economic recovery and livelihood restoration for affected communities, Psychological support for victims, Legal and Policy Aspects of Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) in Mining: Integration of DRR into environmental impact assessments and mine closure plans, Importance of robust regulatory oversight, Community-Based Disaster Management (CBDM): Empowering local communities in hazard identification, preparedness, and response, Ethical Considerations and Future Directions: Corporate responsibility in disaster prevention and response. Accountability for environmental damages, Climate change and its implications for mining hazards (e.g., extreme rainfall, droughts), Role of technology (AI, IoT, Big Data) in future disaster management.

unit1_text: UNIT 1: INTRODUCTION TO MINE LEGISLATION & REGULATORY FRAMEWORK Historical Evolution of Mine Legislation in India: Pre-independence regulations, post-independence acts, international influences (e.g., ILO conventions).  Constitutional Provisions Related to Mines: Entry 54 of Union List, State List, Concurrent List – powers of Central and State Governments. The Mines Act, 1952: Objectives and scope of the Act, Definitions of key terms (mine, owner, agent, manager, competent person, serious bodily injury, etc.), Provisions related to health, safety, and welfare of workers, Employment of women and young persons, Notifiable diseases and accidents, Duties and responsibilities of owners, agents, and managers, Penalties for contravention. The Mines Rules, 1955: General provisions related to health and sanitation (drinking water, latrines, first aid), Provisions related to medical examination and certificates, Duties of workmen. Introduction to Key Regulatory Bodies: Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS) – historical background, organizational structure, powers, and functions.
unit2_text: UNIT 2: MINE SAFETY MANAGEMENT & HAZARDS IN MINES Principles of Mine Safety Management: Safety policy, safety organization, safety audit, safety management plan (SMP). Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) in Mines: Techniques and methodologies for identifying hazards, assessing risks, and implementing control measures. Major Hazards in Underground Mines: Ground Control: Roof falls, side falls, rock bursts, strata movement. Causes, prevention, and support systems, Explosions: Methane explosions, coal dust explosions. General Electrical Safety in Mines: Definitions (e.g., intrinsic safety, flameproof enclosure). Earthing practices, Protection against overcurrent, short circuit, and earth leakage, Insulation and cabling. Statutory Provisions for Electrical Installations: The Electricity Act, 2003 (relevant sections) and the Central Electricity Authority (Measures Relating to Safety and Electric Supply) Regulations, 2010 (relevant to mines). Accident Reporting and Investigation: Statutory requirements for reporting accidents, Principles of accident investigation: data collection, root cause analysis, recommendations, Role of DGMS in accident investigation. Occupational Health & Hygiene in Mines: Common occupational diseases (pneumoconiosis, silicosis, noise-induced hearing loss), Prevention and control measures, Health surveillance. Role of Trade Unions and Workers' Participation in Safety. Recent Amendments and Future Trends in Mine Safety Legislation.

unit1_text: [07 Hours] Power Generation & Transmission in Mines Mechanical Power Transmission: belt drives, chain drives and gear drives; couplings (rigid, flexible, fluid); clutches and brakes used in mining machinery; basic selection criteria for mining duty. Hydraulic Power Systems: fundamentals of hydrostatic and hydrodynamic transmission; hydraulic fluids; hydraulic pumps (gear, vane, piston), motors, cylinders and accumulators; directional, pressure and flow-control valves; hydraulic couplings and torque converters; applications in mines. Pneumatic Power and Compressed Air: principles of compression; single-stage and multi-stage reciprocating compressors; rotary and screw compressors (overview); intercoolers, after-coolers, receivers and unloading arrangement; layout of compressed-air pipelines; transmission losses; in-bye compressors.
unit2_text: [08 Hours] Wire Ropes & Haulage Systems Wire Ropes: applications in surface and underground mines; construction, lays, classification (round-strand, locked-coil, non-stranded, flattened-strand); factor of safety; examination, testing, care and maintenance; capping (white-metal and resin) and splicing; rope capels; rope-changing procedure. Track Haulage: direct, endless, main-and-tail and gravity haulage systems; pull and power calculations; safety devices — Lilly controller, stop blocks, runaway switches, drag, manholes and refuge holes. Locomotive Haulage: trolley-wire, diesel, battery and flameproof locomotives; track laying and maintenance; mine cars and tubs; productivity calculations for haulage systems.
unit3_text: [08 Hours] Conveyors, Aerial Ropeways & Hoisting Systems Belt Conveyors: construction and main components — drums, idlers, pulleys, fabric and steel-cord belting; drive arrangements; tensioning devices (gravity, screw, hydraulic take-up); loading and discharge arrangements; safety and sequence-control devices; capacity and power calculations; splicing and maintenance. Chain Conveyors: armoured face conveyor (AFC) and panzer conveyor — construction, drive units, chain types and applicability at longwall faces; scraper-chain and shaker conveyors — construction and application. Aerial Ropeways: monocable and bicable systems; construction, layout, rope-tensioning and applications. Hoisting — Shaft Arrangement: headgear, shaft fittings; cages, skips and their suspension gear; detaching hooks; principal safety devices.
unit4_text: [09 Hours] Winding Systems and Face / Development Machinery Drum Winders: cylindrical and conical drums; winding cycles; mechanical and electrical braking (dynamic, regenerative and plugging). Electric Winders: AC and DC drives; speed control (overview); safety circuits and interlocks. Koepe Winding: ground-mounted and tower-mounted Koepe winders; single and multi-rope friction winding; comparison with drum winding. Winding Calculations: torque–time and power–time diagrams; horse-power requirement; selection of winder for given duty cycle. Drilling Machines: jack-hammers, jumbos, drifters and wagon drills; rotary coal drills; DTH and rotary blast-hole drills for opencast mining; selection criteria and productivity assessment. Coal Cutting & Cutter Loaders: conventional coal cutters and ploughs; single-ended and double-ended ranging-drum shearer (DERDS); interface with powered supports. Road Headers: boom-type road headers; rock-tool interaction; selection based on rock strength. Underground Loading & Transport: rocker shovel, gathering-arm loader, side-discharge loader (SDL), load-haul-dump (LHD), shuttle cars and underground trucks; productivity calculation; continuous miner systems. Surface Mining Equipment: rope shovel, hydraulic excavator, dragline (with range-diagram concept), bucket-wheel excavator, continuous surface miner, scrapers, dozers, front-end loaders; productivity calculation for shovel–dumper combination.
unit5_text: [08 Hours] Mine Drainage Pumps and Comminution Machinery Mine Drainage: sources of mine water; drainage planning; dewatering of opencast and underground mines. Types of Mine Pumps: reciprocating, centrifugal (single-stage and multi-stage), turbine, submersible, sinking pumps and sludge pumps; pump fittings and ranging arrangements. Pump Characteristics: head–discharge, power and efficiency curves; net positive suction head (NPSH) and cavitation; series and parallel operation; pump selection for given duty. Comminution Theories: Rittinger's, Kick's and Bond's laws; energy considerations and grindability indices. Crushers: jaw, gyratory, cone and roll crushers — construction, operation and selection criteria. Grinding Mills: ball, rod, tube and pebble mills; critical speed; open and closed-circuit grinding (overview).

subject_name_print: Subject Code: BMN-072 Mine Safety Engineering
university_name: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University, Lucknow
co1_text: Explain the types, causes and investigation of mine accidents, accident statistics, and the essential elements of a mine safety-management system.
co2_text: Analyse the hazards arising from mine gases, fires and explosions, and select appropriate detection, monitoring and control measures.
co3_text: Apply dust-control, illumination, inundation-control and occupational-health measures to safeguard the health and safety of mine workers.
co4_text: Apply fault-tree analysis, probabilistic risk analysis and reliability concepts to identify, assess and manage risks in mines.
co5_text: Explain the statutory framework, rescue and recovery practice, and disaster-management measures applicable to Indian mines.
unit1_text: [08 Hours] Mine Accidents, Accident Analysis and Safety Management Mine Accidents: occupational hazards of mining; accidents in mines — different types and classification; accident investigation; accident proneness; basic causes of accident occurrence; place-wise and cause-wise analysis. Accident Statistics & Costs: frequency and severity rates of accidents; accident-data analysis and assessment; relation between accidents and efficiency; direct and indirect cost of accidents. Safety Management: creating and maintaining safety awareness; ZAP and MAP; job safety analysis; safety meetings and committees; management’s role and responsibility; introduction to risk-based safety and health management systems; safety management plan; measures for improving safety in mines.
unit2_text: [08 Hours] Underground Hazards I — Mine Gases, Fires and Explosions Mine Gases: composition of the mine atmosphere; production, properties and physiological effects of mine gases; sampling and analysis of mine air; methane content and methane layering; methane drainage; flame safety lamp and methanometers; radon and its daughter products; continuous monitoring of gases. Mine Fires: causes and classification of mine fires; spontaneous combustion — mechanism, stages and susceptibility indices; factors affecting spontaneous heating; detection and prevention; dealing with mine fires by direct and indirect methods; fire stoppings and sealing-off; re-opening of sealed-off areas; fires in coal stacks and waste dumps. Mine Explosions: firedamp and coal-dust explosions — causes, mechanism and prevention; explosive limits; stone-dust and water barriers; explosions in opencast workings; investigation after an explosion.
unit3_text: [08 Hours] Underground Hazards II — Dust, Inundation, Illumination and Occupational Health Airborne Dust: generation, dispersion, measurement and control of airborne respirable dust; sampling instruments and methods, duration and interval of sampling; prevention and suppression of dust; physiological effects of dust and dust-related diseases (pneumoconiosis, silicosis). Inundation: causes and prevention of inundation; precautions and techniques in approaching old workings; dewatering of waterlogged workings; safety boring apparatus and pattern of holes; design and construction of water dams. Illumination & Occupational Health: standards of illumination for underground and opencast workings; cap lamps; lamp-room layout and organisation; photometry and illumination survey; comfort conditions, first aid and ambulance; miners’ occupational diseases — causes, nature and preventive measures; preventive medical examinations and compensable diseases.
unit4_text: [08 Hours] Risk Assessment and Safety-Engineering Techniques Risk Assessment: principles of risk assessment; hazard identification; risk and hazard control; risk and hazard evaluation; data collection for identified health risks; exposure assessment and risk characterisation; methods of risk assessment. Fault-Tree Analysis: introduction and methodology; symbols and Boolean techniques; qualitative analysis; computerised methods; statistical analysis and safety information; systems design. Reliability & Safety Audit: probabilistic risk analysis; reliability evaluation; human factors; safety culture; safety audit and its application to mine-safety problems.
unit5_text: [08 Hours] Mine Legislation, Rescue, Recovery and Disaster Management Mine Legislation: the Mines Act, 1952; the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017; the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961; statutory controls and directions; spot and regular inspections; enforcement of standards and penalties for violations; role of the Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS); safety campaigns and Safety Week. Rescue & Recovery: rescue equipment and its uses; classification of rescue apparatus; resuscitation; rescue stations and rescue rooms; organisation of rescue work; emergency preparedness and response systems; Mines Rescue Rules and Mines Vocational Training Rules. Disaster Management: identification of causes of mine disasters; preventive action; disaster management and mitigation; typical cases of mine disasters in India; recommendations of inquiry committees on safety and health issues.

subject_name_print: Subject Code: BMN-073 Mine Automation & Data Analytics
university_name: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University, Lucknow
co1_text: Explain the essential elements, principles and strategies of mine automation and the working of autonomous mining, fleet-management and remote-operation systems.
co2_text: Make use of automated communication, tracking, sensing and virtual-reality technologies for implementing automation and ensuring safe operations in mines.
co3_text: Apply descriptive and inferential statistics and fundamental machine-learning concepts to analyse mining data.
co4_text: Analyse mining data using supervised learning, artificial neural networks and deep-learning techniques.
co5_text: Apply unsupervised learning, big-data analytics and artificial intelligence to mining decision-making and optimisation problems.
unit1_text: [08 Hours] Foundations of Mine Automation and Autonomous Systems Automation Fundamentals: essential elements of an automated system; automation in the mine production system; principles and strategies of automation; introduction to automation productivity and levels of automation. Autonomous Mining Systems: autonomous haulage systems (AHS); automated drilling systems; tele-remote and autonomous operating modes; selection considerations for autonomous equipment. Fleet Management & Remote Operations: Fleet Management Systems — Truck Dispatch System (TDS), Computerised Maintenance Management System (CMMS) and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) for the mining industry; mine remote operations and control; mining robotics and “armchair mining”; remote operating centres.
unit2_text: [08 Hours] Sensing, Communication, Tracking and Virtual-Reality Technologies Automated Communication & Tracking Technologies: proximity-detection systems; GNSS/UPS positioning; radar systems; RFID and geo-fencing; CCD cameras and machine vision; image processing; SCADA architecture and its applications in mines. Virtual Reality & Simulation: virtual-reality applications in mining; mining-equipment concept development; mine-safety training applications; mining-operation simulations and visualisation of the mining process for safe operations.
unit3_text: [08 Hours] Statistical Foundations and Introduction to Machine Learning Descriptive Statistics: measures of central tendency and dispersion; data summarisation and visualisation; probability and probability distributions (discrete and continuous) relevant to mining data. Inferential Statistics: sampling and estimation; hypothesis testing; regression analysis; analysis of variance (ANOVA); interpretation of results for mining problems. Introduction to Machine Learning: basic concepts, terminology and the learning workflow; supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning; the data-analytics pipeline for mining applications.
unit4_text: [08 Hours] Supervised Learning, Neural Networks and Deep Learning Supervised Learning: classification and regression; feature engineering; training, validation and testing; the bias–variance trade-off; model-evaluation metrics. Artificial Neural Networks: the perceptron and multilayer networks; activation functions; the back-propagation algorithm; network training and regularisation. Deep Learning: deep network architectures (overview); representation and feature learning; representative applications of deep learning to mining and geoscience data.
unit5_text: [08 Hours] Unsupervised Learning, Big-Data Analytics and AI Applications in Mining Unsupervised Learning: clustering techniques; pattern and structure discovery in unlabelled mining data; dimensionality reduction (overview). Big-Data Analytics: characteristics and challenges of big data; data acquisition, storage and management; analytics frameworks and pipelines for large-scale mining data. Applications in Mining: application of big-data analytics and artificial intelligence in mining — predictive maintenance, production and energy optimisation, safety analytics and decision-support systems.

co1_text: Classify mineral resources and reserves as per UNFC; carry out sampling and grade-reserve estimation for mineral deposits.
co2_text: Apply standard methods of mine valuation (Hoskold's, Morkill's, present-value) and compute depreciation and capital recovery for mining assets.
co3_text: Evaluate mining investment proposals using discounted and non-discounted cash flow methods and perform sensitivity analysis.
co4_text: Explain principles of financial management of mining enterprises and apply provisions of mineral taxation under MMDR Act and related rules.
co5_text: Prepare profit-and-loss account, balance sheet and cost-of-production statements; demonstrate awareness of National Mineral Policy and sustainable mining.
unit1_text: [06 Hours] Mineral Resources, Reserves and Sampling Resource and Reserve Classification: concepts; IBM and UNFC frameworks; JORC and CRIRSCO codes; measured, indicated and inferred resources; proved, probable and possible reserves. Sampling and Statistical Analysis: grab, channel, chip, bulk and drill-core sampling; sample preparation and reduction; salting and precautions; statistical treatment — mean, variance and standard error of grade. Grade and Reserve Estimation: cut-off grade and break-even grade; reserve estimation by cross-section, polygonal, triangular and inverse-distance methods; introduction to geostatistics and kriging; grade-tonnage curve.
unit2_text: [07 Hours] Mine Valuation Valuation Fundamentals: objectives and scope of mine valuation; factors affecting mine value; valuation for sale, taxation and mortgage; distinction between mine, accounting and market valuation. Methods of Mine Valuation: present-value method; Hoskold's, Morkill's and O'Donahue formulae; replacement-cost and comparative methods; relative merits and limitations. Life and Capacity of a Mine: Taylor's rule for optimum capacity; relationship between reserve, capacity and life; effect of cut-off grade on life and capacity. Depreciation and Capital Recovery: straight-line, declining-balance, sum-of-years-digits, sinking-fund and production-unit methods; amortization of intangibles; redemption of capital; depletion allowance.
unit3_text: [09 Hours] Discounted Cash Flow Analysis Time Value of Money: compounding and discounting; present value, future value, annuity and perpetuity; effect of compounding frequency. Cash Flow Analysis: project cash flow diagrams; project life cycle — exploration, development, production and closure; treatment of escalation, inflation and working capital; tax-affected cash flow. Investment Appraisal Methods: non-discounted methods — payback period and accounting rate of return; discounted methods — NPV, IRR, discounted payback, profitability index, B/C ratio, modified IRR; conflict between NPV and IRR for ranking. Sensitivity and Risk Analysis: one-way sensitivity (spider and tornado diagrams); scenario analysis; Monte-Carlo simulation (overview); risk-adjusted discount rate. Project Selection: ranking of mutually exclusive projects; capital rationing; replacement decisions; case studies on mining-project appraisal.
unit4_text: [09 Hours] Financial Management and Mineral Taxation Business Organization and Financing: forms of business organization; memorandum and articles of association; sources of short-term and long-term capital for mining enterprises. Capital Structure: equity shares, preference shares, debentures, retained earnings and term loans; cost of capital; weighted average cost of capital (WACC); leverage. Break-Even and Inventory: break-even chart, break-even point, margin of safety and contribution margin; ABC analysis, Economic Order Quantity (EOQ), reorder level and safety stock. Mineral Taxation: royalty (tonnage and ad-valorem); dead rent; cess — District Mineral Foundation (DMF) and National Mineral Exploration Trust (NMET); income tax on mining; GST impact; MMDR Act 1957 (as amended in 2015 and 2021); Mineral Concession Rules 2016. Mineral Pricing: factors governing mineral prices; primary versus secondary markets; price volatility and cyclical nature of the mineral economy; long-term contracts versus spot markets; commodity exchanges.
unit5_text: [05 Hours] Financial Statements and Mineral Economics in Practice Book-Keeping Essentials: double-entry system; journal, ledger and subsidiary books; trial balance; rectification of errors. Financial Statements: preparation of profit-and-loss account and balance sheet; key financial ratios — current ratio, debt-equity, ROCE and earnings per share. Cost of Production: cost classification — fixed, variable, direct, indirect and overhead; cost per tonne; cost centres in a mine. Mineral Economics in Industry: National Mineral Policy 2019; pre-feasibility, feasibility and bankable feasibility studies; sustainable mining and ESG reporting (overview).

prerequisites: RVE 301/401- Universal Human Values and Professional Ethics
co1_text: Understand the basic concepts of Madhyasth Darshan
co2_text: Understand the human being, the needs and activities of human being through Madhyasth Darshan
co3_text: Understand the whole existence
co4_text: Understand the role of human being in the entire existence, thus getting clarity about values at all levels of living and human conduct
co5_text: Understand the foundation of human society and human tradition.
unit1_text:
I
Introduction to Madhyasth Darshan and its Basics Need
to study Madhyasth Darshan; introduction, basic
formulations of the darshan; the complete expanse of
study and the natural outcome of living according to the
darshan.
unit2_text:
II
Submergence of Nature in Space
The ever-present existence in the form of nature
submerged in space; nature classified into two
categories – material and consciousness, and four
orders; the form, property, natural characteristic and
selforganization of the four orders, General direction
and process of evolution in the nature/ existence.
unit3_text:
III
Human Being as an indivisible part of Nature
Human being as an indivisible part of nature; various
types (five classes) of human beings; human being in
the combination of self and body; purpose of self as
realization, prosperity for the body; need of behavior
and work for attaining the goals of realization and
prosperity
unit4_text:
IV
Fulfillment of human goal of realization and prosperity
Following natural, social and psychological principles
for actualizing the human goal; form of conducive
society and order for such practices, study process-
achieving realization through self-study and practice
while living in such a society (social order).
unit5_text:
V
Human Conduct based on Madhyasth Darshan
Description of such a realized self, continuity of
happiness, peace, satisfaction and bliss through
realization, conduct of a realized human being.
Possibility of finding solutions to present day problems
(such as inequality of rich and poor, man and woman
etc.) in the light of it.
