Portfolio concept and diversification; Modern Portfolio Theory (Markowitz model); Efficient Frontier; 
CAPM framework; risk-return optimization; asset allocation strategies; active vs passive investment 
strategies; behavioural aspects of investing.
unit5_text:
Module V: Portfolio Performance Evaluation (6 Hours) 
Performance evaluation techniques; Sharpe Ratio, Treynor Ratio, Jensen’s Alpha; risk-adjusted return 
measures; portfolio revision and rebalancing; measurement of systematic and unsystematic risk; 
interpretation of portfolio outcomes; investor behaviour and decision biases.

leasing, hire purchase, credit rating and securitisation.

discounting to business financing situations.

unit1_text:
Module I: Financial System and Market Structure (10 Hours) 
Financial system: meaning, structure, functions, and significance; financial intermediation and role of 
intermediaries; money market instruments (Treasury Bills, CPs, CDs, call money, MMMFs); capital 
market structure; primary and secondary markets; IPOs, book building, rights issue, bonus issue; stock 
exchanges (NSE, BSE); trading mechanisms, settlement cycle (T+2), demat system; SEBI role and 
regulatory framework; investor protection mechanisms; Digital Financial Ecosystem in India (UPI, 
NEFT, IMPS architecture overview); Digital wallets and payment gateways; Introduction to Digital 
Banking and Neo-banks.
unit2_text:
Module II: Leasing and Hire Purchase (8 Hours) 
Concept of leasing; types of leases; lease evaluation from lessee and lessor perspectives; advantages and 
limitations; tax implications; buy vs lease decision-making; hire purchase system; comparison between 
hire purchase and installment purchase; major leasing institutions in India and their role in financial 
decision-making; Introduction to Blockchain and smart contracts in leasing agreements.
unit3_text:
Module III: Mutual Funds and Credit Rating (8 Hours) 
Mutual funds: structure, types, advantages, and limitations; NAV calculation; SIP and SWP; entry and 
exit loads; mutual fund regulation in India; credit rating agencies; rating process, symbols, and 
methodology; role and importance of credit ratings in investment decisions; Robo-advisory, Algorithm 
credits and AI-based portfolio recommendations
unit4_text:
Module IV: Securitisation and Financial Services (6 Hours) 
Concept of securitisation; process and structure; benefits and limitations; overview of financial services 
industry; fund-based vs fee-based services; role of financial intermediaries in service delivery; 
introduction to structured financial products in modern markets; Introduction to tokenisation of financial 
assets and RegTech (Regulatory Technology) for compliance automation.
unit5_text:
Module V: Factoring, Forfaiting and Bill Discounting (8 Hours) 
Factoring: meaning, types (recourse/non-recourse), domestic and international factoring; cost structure 
and process; bill discounting and rediscounting; forfaiting: mechanism, features, and applications; 
comparative analysis of factoring, forfaiting, and bill discounting; practical applications and numerical 
problems.

Module V: Advanced Forecasting and Financial Decision Models (7 Hours) 
Introduction to Autocorrelation and Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA); model 
selection and validation; comparative forecasting methods; financial interpretation of forecasts for 
strategic decision-making.

Forward Rate Agreements (FRAs); interest rate swaps; currency swaps; Credit Default Swaps (CDS); 
overview of structured credit instruments; role of derivatives in global financial markets; basic 
understanding of financial crises linked to derivatives.
unit5_text:
Module V: Applications of Derivatives in Risk Management (8 Hours) 
Risk exposure in business; hedging strategies using forwards, futures, and options; commodity and 
currency risk management; evaluation of hedging effectiveness; real-world applications of derivatives in 
corporate decision-making.

domains.

unit1_text:
Module I Strategic Management & Corporate Governance (5 Hours) 
Introduction: Meaning, nature, scope, and importance of strategy; Model of Strategic Management; Strategic Decision-
Making Process. Corporate Governance: Composition of the Board; Role and Responsibilities of the Board of Directors; 
Trends in Corporate Governance; Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR). Case Studies and Latest Updates.
unit2_text:
Module II: Models of Environmental Scanning  (9 Hours) 
Environmental Scanning: Understanding the Macro Environment: PESTEL Analysis; Industrial Organization (IO) & the 
Structure Conduct Performance (SCP) Approach; Porter’s Five Forces Model; Understanding the Micro Environment: 
Resource-Based View (RBV) Analysis; VRIO Framework; Using Resources to Gain Competitive Advantage & its 
Sustainability; Value Chain Analysis. Case Studies and Latest Updates.
unit3_text:
Module III: Strategy Formulation (10 Hours) 
Strategy Formulation: Situational Analysis using SWOT Approach. Business Strategies: Competitive Strategy – Cost 
Leadership, Differentiation & Focus; Cooperative Strategy – Collusion & Strategic Alliances. Corporate Strategies: 
Directional Strategy – Growth Strategies, Stability Strategies & Retrenchment Strategies; Corporate Parenting. 
Functional Strategies: Marketing, Financial, R&D, Operations, Purchasing, Logistics, HRM & IT. The Sourcing Decision: 
Outsourcing & Offshoring. Case Studies and Latest Updates.
unit4_text:
Module IV: Strategy Implementation (10 Hours) 
Strategy Choice and Analysis: Scenario Analysis Process; Tools & Techniques of Strategic Analysis: BCG Matrix; Ansoff 
Grid; GE Nine Cell Planning Grid; McKinsey’s 7’S Framework. Strategy Implementation: Developing Programs, Budget 
and Procedures; Stages of Corporate Development; Organizational Life Cycle; Organizational Structures: Matrix, 
Network & Modular/Cellular; Reengineering and Strategy Implementation; Leadership and Corporate Culture. Case 
Studies and Latest Updates.
unit5_text:
Module V: Strategy Evaluation and Control  (6 Hours) 
Strategy Evaluation & Control: Evaluation & Control Process; Measuring Performance: Types of Controls; Activity-Based 
Costing; Enterprise Risk Management; Primary Measures of Corporate Performance; Balanced Scorecard Approach to 
Measure Key Performance; Responsibility Centers; Benchmarking; Problems in Measuring Performance & Guidelines 
for Proper Control. Strategic Audit of a Corporation; Case Studies and Latest Updates.

unit1_text:
Unit- I (Session 06) 
Global Financial Environment: Objective of financial management in a multinational 
corporation, functions of international financial management. Special decision variables in 
international financial management. International monetary system, Fischer Effect, International 
fisher effect.
unit2_text:
Unit -II (Session 10) 
Management of exposure and risk: Concept of exposure and risk. Types of exposure – 
transaction, transnational and economic exposure. Measurement of transaction exposure. 
Managing transaction exposure. Hedging Strategies. 
International Portfolio Investment: Economic determinants. The national FDI policy 
framework. Benefits of inter-national equity and bond investing. International capital asset 
pricing model (ICAPM)
unit3_text:
Unit -III (Session 08) 
International Capital Budgeting: The basic framework for analysis. Issues and strategic 
considerations in international capital budgeting. The adjusted present value approach (APV). 
Financial risk and cost of capital. Exchange risk and cost of capital. Political risk and cost of 
capital. Impact of hedging on cost of capital. Tax consideration – Branch vs. subsidiary, 
withholding tax. Foreign sales corporations, 80-20 subsidiaries and tax havens.
unit4_text:
Unit- IV (Session 08) 
International working capital management: 
i) International cash management: The cash positioning decision. Advantages and disadvantages 
of centralized cash management. Multilateral netting. Intra corporate transfer of funds. 
Transfer pricing, problems of international cash management. 
ii) International Receivables management: Domestic v/s International receivables management. 
Letter of credit. International factoring and Accounts receivables. 
iii) International inventory management: Advance inventory purchases. Stockpiling.
unit5_text:
Unit -V (Session 08) 
International Financing Decisions: 
i) Euro-money and Eurobond Markets. Size of the Euro currency market. Growth of Euro Dollar 
market. Instruments and rate of Euro Currency Markets. Creation of Euro deposits. Syndicated 
Eurocurrency loan Market. International Bond Markets, Multi-currency bonds and their types. 
Rationale for multi currency bonds. 
ii)  International Equity markets: Foreign equity market and their comparative performance. 
Recent developments and innovations in international capital markets. Recent developments in 
the Euro bond market.

Managing the Supply Pipeline for Global Trade Flows, The Global Logistics Operators, 
Comparison between National and International Logistics, International Transport System, 
Globalisation and International Trade Environment. Factors Driving Global Supply Chain 
Management, Customs and Global Supply Chain Management. Case Studies and Latest 
Updates
unit2_text:
Export Sales Contract in International Logistics (8 Hours) 
Constituents of the Export Sales Contract, Contract of Affreightment: Terms of Delivery & 
Incoterms standards. International Purchasing Systems- Constituents, Strategy and its 
Interface with the Management of the Global Supply Chain, Negotiating the Contract, 
Selecting the International Logistics Operator, Criteria of Selecting the Third-Party Logistics 
Operator. Case Studies and Latest Updates

& Trade-Off. Considerations of Speed, Frequency, Packing and Insurance in International 
Transportation. Warehousing & Benchmarking in Global Supply Chain Management, 
Supply Chain Cycle Time Reduction, Demand-Driven Supply Network in International 
Logistics. Case Studies and Latest Updates.

International Transport Systems (7 Hours) 
Introduction to International Transport System- Basic Terms, Characteristics and Relations, 
Significance of Transportation Services, Characteristics of Modes of Transports -Road 
Transportation, Rail Transportation, Maritime Transport, Air Transport. Technical 
performance & Transport Economic Indicators, Maritime Routing Patterns, The 
Containerization of Commodities, Transcontinental Bridges. Case Studies and Latest 
Updates.
unit5_text:
Cost and Economy of International Logistics (7 Hours) 
International Transport and Economic Development, Transportation and Commercial 
Geography, Components of International Transport Costs, International Transport Supply 
and Demand, Location Analysis, Market Area Analysis, The Nature of International 
Transport Policy, International Transport Planning, International Transport Safety and 
Security, Traffic Counts and Traffic Surveys, Cost / Benefit Analysis. Case Studies and 
Latest Updates.

unit1_text:
Basic Concepts and principles: Definition, Nature and Scope of Economics-Micro Economics and 
Macro Economics, Managerial Economics and its relevance in business decisions. Fundamental Principles of 
Managerial Economics - Incremental Principle, Marginal Principle, Opportunity Cost Principle, Discounting 
Principle, Concept of Time Perspective, Equi-Marginal Principle, Utility Analysis, Cardinal Utility and Ordinal 
Utility. Case Studies
unit2_text:
Demand and Supply Analysis: Theory of Demand, Types of Demand. Determinants of demand, 
Demand Function, Demand Schedule, Demand curve, Law of Demand, Exceptions to the law of Demand, 
Shifts in demand curve, Elasticity of Demand and its measurement. Price Elasticity, Income Elasticity, Arc 
Elasticity. Cross Elasticity and Advertising Elasticity. Uses of Elasticity of Demand for managerial decision 
making, Demand forecasting meaning, significance and methods. ( numerical Exercises) Case Studies 
Supply Analysis; Law of Supply, Supply Elasticity; Analysis and its uses for managerial decision making. 
Price of a Product under demand and supply forces . Case Studies
unit3_text:
Production and cost Analysis: Production concepts & analysis; Production function, Types of production 
function, Laws of production: Law of diminishing returns, Law of returns to scale. Cost concept and analysis: 
Cost, Types of costs, Cost output relationship in the short-run. Cost output relationship in the Long-run. 
Estimation of revenue. Average Revenue, Marginal Revenue. Case Studies
unit4_text:
Market  structures: Perfect  and  Imperfect  Market  Structures,  Perfect  Competition,  features, 
determination of price under perfect competition. Monopoly: Feature, pricing under monopoly, Price 
Discrimination. Monopolistic: Features, pricing under monopolistic competition, product differentiation. 
Oligopoly: Features, kinked demand curve, cartels, price leadership. Case Studies
unit5_text:
National Income; Concepts and various methods of its measurement, Circular flows in 2 sector, 3 sector,4 
sector economies, Inflation, types and causes, Business Cycle & its phases.

unit1_text:
Unit I (10 Hrs): Descriptive Statistics 
Meaning, Scope, types, functions and limitations of statistics, Measures of Central tendency– Mean, 
Median, Mode, Quartiles, Measures of Dispersion – Range, Inter quartile range, Mean deviation, Standard 
deviation, Variance, Coefficient of Variation, Skewness and Kurtosis.
unit2_text:
Unit II (8 Hrs):Time Series & Index Number 
Time series analysis: Concept, Additive and Multiplicative models, Components of time series, 
Trend  analysis:  Least  Square  method  -  Linear  and  Non-  Linear  equations,  Applications  in business 
decision-making. 
Index Numbers:- Meaning , Types of index numbers, uses of index numbers, Construction of Price, Quantity 
and Volume indices:-Fixed base and Chain base methods.
unit3_text:
Unit III (6 Hrs): Correlation & Regression Analysis 
Correlation  Analysis: Rank Method & Karl Pearson's Coefficient of Correlation and Properties Of Correlation. 
Regression Analysis: Fitting of a Regression Line and Interpretation of Results, Properties of 
Regression Coefficients and Relationship between Regression and Correlation.
unit4_text:
Unit IV ( 8 Hrs): Probability Theory & Distribution 
Probability: Theory of Probability, Addition and Multiplication Law, Baye’s Theorem 
Probability  Theoretical  Distributions:  Concept  and  application  of  Binomial;  Poisson  and 
Normal distributions.
unit5_text:
Unit V (8 Hrs) Hypothesis Testing& Business Analytics 
Hypothesis Testing: Null and Alternative Hypotheses; Type I and Type II errors; Testing of Hypothesis: Large 
Sample Tests, Small Sample test, (t, F, Z Test and Chi Square Test) 
Concept of Business Analytics- Meaning types and application of Business Analytics, Use of Spread 
Sheet to anlayze data-Descriptive analytics and Predictive analytics.

unit1_text:
Unit 1 (8 Sessions) 
Research: – Definition, Meaning, Importance types and Qualities of Research; Research applications 
in functional areas of Business, Emerging trends in Business research. Research & the Scientific 
Method: Characteristics of scientific method. Steps in Research Process Concept of Scientific 
Enquiry: – Formulation of Research Problem – Management Question – research Question – 
Investigation Question ,Research Proposal – Elements of a Research Proposal, Drafting a 
Research Proposal, evaluating a research proposal.
unit2_text:
Unit 2 (8 Sessions) 
Research design: Concept, Features of a good research design, Use of a good research 
design; Qualitative and Quantitative research approaches, Comparison – Pros and Cons of both 
approaches. 
Exploratory Research Design: Concept, Types: Qualitative techniques – Projective Techniques, 
Depth Interview, Experience Survey, Focus Groups, Observation. 
Descriptive Research Designs: Concept, types and uses. Concept of Cross-sectional and 
Longitudinal Research ; Experimental Design: Concept of Cause, Causal relationships, Concept of 
Independent & Dependent variables, concomitant variable, extraneous variable, Treatment, Control 
group.
unit3_text:
Unit 3 (6 Sessions) 
Scaling & measurement techniques: Concept of Measurement: Need of Measurement; Problems 
in measurement in management research – Validity and Reliability. Levels of measurement – 
Nominal, Ordinal, Interval, Ratio. Attitude Scaling Techniques: Concept of Scale – Rating Scales 
viz. Likert Scales, Semantic Differential Scales, Constant Sum Scales, Graphic Rating Scales – 
Ranking Scales – Paired comparison & Forced Ranking – Concept and Application.
unit4_text:
Unit 4 (6 Sessions) 
Sampling: Basic Concepts: Defining the Universe, Concepts of Statistical Population, Sample, 
Characteristics of a good sample. Sampling Frame (practical approach for determining the sample 
frame expected), Sampling errors, Non Sampling errors, Methods to reduce the errors, Sample Size 
constraints, Non Response. 
Probability Sample: Simple Random Sample, Systematic Sample, Stratified Random Sample, Area 
Sampling & Cluster Sampling. 
 Non Probability Sample: Judgment Sampling, Convenience Sampling, Purposive  Sampling,  
Quota Sampling & Snowballing Sampling methods. Determining size of the sample – Practical 
considerations in sampling and sample size, sample size determination.
unit5_text:
Unit 5 (8 Sessions) 
Data Analysis: Editing, Coding, Tabular representation of data, frequency tables, Construction of 
frequency distributions, Graphical Representation of Data: Appropriate Usage of Bar charts, Pie 
charts, Histogram. 
Hypothesis: Qualities of a good Hypothesis –Framing Null Hypothesis & Alternative Hypothesis. 
Concept of Hypothesis Testing – Logic & Importance. Analysis of Variance: One way and two way 
Classifications. 
Mechanism of Report Writing- Report Preparation: Types, Report Structure: preliminary section, 
main report, interpretation of results, suggestions and recommendations, limitations of the study, 
Report formulation.

Linear programming: Mathematical formulations of LP Models for product-mix problems; graphical and
simplex method of solving LP problems; duality.
Transportation problem: Various methods of finding Initial basic feasible solution-North West Corner Method,
Least Cost Method & VAM Method and optimal solution-Stepping Stone & MODI Method, Maximization
Transportation Problem

Odds Method; Dominance Method and Graphical Method for solving Mixed Strategy Game.

Sequencing Problem:  Johnsons Algorithm for n Jobs and Two machines, n Jobs and Three Machines, Two jobs

in estimating arrival rate and service rate; Applications of Queue model for better service to the customers.

Replacement Problem: Replacement of assets that deteriorate with time, replacement of assets which fail
suddenly.
Project Management:  Rules for drawing the network diagram, Applications of CPM and PERT techniques in
Project planning and control; crashing of operations.

UNIT I (8 Lectures)
Supply Chain: Supply chain Management in Agriculture, Overview of Supply Chain Components,
Stakeholders in the Agricultural Supply Chain, Linkages between Producers, Processors, Distributors, and
Retailers , Agricultural Marketing in India, Defects in Present System of Agri Marketing ,Case Studies
unit2_text:

Demand Management in Supply Chain: Types of Demand, Demand Planning and Forecasting;
Operations Management in Supply Chain, Basic Principles of Manufacturing Management. Demand
forecasting, functions of inventory, warehousing and distribution centres, transportation, protective
packaging, order processing, material handling with special reference to Agri products
unit3_text:

Management, Material Requirements Planning, Just in Time (JIT), Vendor Managed Inventory
unit4_text:

Logistics Management: History and Evolution of Logistics; Elements of Logistics; Management;
Distribution Management, Distribution Strategies; Pool Distribution; Transportation Management; Fleet
Management; Service Innovation; Warehousing; Packaging for Logistics, Third-Party Logistics
(TPL/3PL); GPS Technology.
unit5_text:
UNIT 5 (8 Lectures)
Concept of Information Technology: IT Application in SCM; Integrated IT solutions for L&SCM,
emerging technologies in L&SCM, Advanced Planning and Scheduling; SCM in Electronic Business; Role
of Knowledge in SCM; Performance Measurement and Controls in Agri. Supply Chain Management-
Benchmarking: introduction, concept and forms of Benchmarking. Logistics & supply chain management
and Information technology in agri business-- from vertical integration to virtual integration, transiting
from made- to- stock to build- to- order.

university_name: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University, Lucknow
co1_text:
Explain the fundamentals of international trade and the structure and 
impact of WTO on agribusiness.
co2_text:
Analyse WTO agreements and trade barriers relevant to sustainable 
agribusiness trade.
co3_text:
Apply key economic trade theories to evaluate India's position in 
global agribusiness trade.
co4_text:
Examine India’s foreign trade policy, its effects on balance of 
payments, and trade performance.
co5_text:
Demonstrate knowledge of export-import procedures, market entry 
strategies, and sustainability in global trade.
unit1_text:
Unit I: Basics of International Trade and WTO (4 Hours) 
Introduction to international trade: concepts and importance; World Trade Organization (WTO): 
structure, functions, and role; Implications of WTO for Indian economy in general and agriculture in 
particular; Overview of global trade environment and challenges for agribusiness
unit2_text:
Unit II: WTO Agreements and Trade Regulations (6 Hours) 
Trade-Related Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS); Trade-Related Investment Measures (TRIMS); 
Quotas, anti-dumping duties, quantitative and qualitative restrictions; Tariff and non-tariff measures, 
trade liberalization; Subsidies, green box and red box measures under WTO; Future negotiation issues 
at WTO; Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) and carbon trading relevance to agribusiness 
sustainability.
unit3_text:
Unit III: Foreign Trade and Economic Theories (10 Hours) 
Importance of foreign trade for developing economies; Concepts of absolute and comparative 
advantage; Overview of India’s foreign trade with special focus on agriculture and agribusiness; 
Emerging trends and challenges in global agribusiness trade
unit4_text:
Unit IV: India’s Foreign Trade Policy and Economic Implications (10 Hours) 
Composition and features of India’s foreign trade policy; India’s balance of payments and its impact 
on trade; Inter-regional vs. international trade; Tariffs, trade controls, and exchange rate mechanisms; 
Foreign trade multiplier and its significance in economic growth; Foreign demand and supply side 
analysis in agribusiness trade; Opportunity cost and implications for developing countries; Trade and 
factor price relationships; Market entry methods for global agribusiness markets.
unit5_text:
Unit V: Export-Import Procedures and Market Entry (10 Hours) 

Export-import documentation and procedures: commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, 
certificate of origin, phytosanitary certificate, export/import license, letter of credit, insurance 
certificate, customs declaration, inspection certificate, consular invoice; Role of government and trade 
facilitation bodies; Logistics and supply chain management including cold chain and transportation; 
Marketing strategies for sustainable global agribusiness markets.

unit1_text: Concept and meaning of agricultural risk; Classification of risks: Variate risks and non-covariate risks; Sources and nature of risks in agriculture
unit2_text:
Unit 2: Types of Agricultural Risks(8 Hours) 
Price risk: fluctuations in market prices of inputs and outputs; Yield risk: variability in crop and 
livestock production; Climate and weather risks: droughts, floods, storms, and weather aberrations; 
Asset risk: risks related to machinery, land, and infrastructure; Health risk: impact on farmers’ health 
and labor capacity
unit3_text:
Unit 3: Impact of Climate Change on Agriculture(8 Hours) 
Effects of climate change and weather aberrations on crop yield; Socio-economic impacts on farming 
communities, with special focus on arid and semi-arid regions; Case studies highlighting regional 
vulnerabilities and adaptation challenges
unit4_text:
Unit 4: Strategies for Agricultural Risk Management(10 Hours) 
Risk identification and assessment techniques; Risk avoidance, reduction, and mitigation strategies; 
Role of diversification, improved agronomic practices, and technology adoption; Designing risk 
management products and programmes tailored for farmers
unit5_text:
Unit 5: Agricultural Insurance and Policy Mechanisms(10 Hours) 
Overview of agricultural insurance schemes and products; Compensation mechanisms and claim 
processes; Legislative and regulatory framework supporting agricultural risk management; Estimation 
of losses and its importance in policy design; Role of government and private sectors in risk 
management and insurance

futures and derivative markets in agribusiness.

co3_text:
Apply trading strategies and techniques for hedging and 
speculation in commodity markets.

Interpret and evaluate commodity price movements using

unit1_text:
UNIT I: Introduction to Commodity and Derivative Markets(6 Hours) 
Commodities and their classifications; Spot markets and agricultural mandis; Concept of 
derivatives; Types of derivatives – forwards, futures, options, swaps; Evolution of 
commodity futures markets; Significance of commodity derivatives in agriculture; Role in 
price discovery and risk management.
unit2_text:
UNIT II: Market Structure and Pricing Mechanisms(10 Hours) 
Need for commodity futures markets; Pricing of commodity futures; Basis and cost of carry; 
Evaluation of international commodity exchanges (CME, NYMEX, LME); Commodity 
futures in India – evolution and growth; Role of NCDEX and MCX; Regulatory framework – 
SEBI and policy reforms; Dynamics of a commodity exchange and trading platforms; Case 
studies.
unit3_text:
UNIT III: Market Participants and Trading Strategies(8 Hours) 
Types of market participants – hedgers, speculators, arbitrageurs; Trading strategies – 
hedging, spreading, speculation; Role of brokers and clearing members; Risk management 
strategies in commodity markets; Margin requirements and risk control measures; Case 
studies.
unit4_text:
UNIT IV: Market Analysis and Decision Tools(8 Hours) 
Fundamental analysis – supply-demand factors, crop reports, weather, government policies; 
Technical analysis – chart patterns, trend lines, moving averages, oscillators; Analyzing 


commodity price chart patterns; Confirming tools – volume analysis, open interest, sentiment 
indicators; Case studies.
unit5_text:
UNIT V: Operations, Clearing and Emerging Trends(8 Hours) 
Trading techniques – straddles, strangles, spreads; Clearing and settlement process; Delivery 
mechanisms – physical and cash settlement; Taxation and accounting issues; Role of 
technology in commodity trading – electronic platforms, algo trading; Global trends in 
commodity derivatives; Case studies.

university_name: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University, Lucknow
co1_text:
Describe the role, stages, and sources of project finance in the context of 
agribusiness.
co2_text:
Conduct feasibility analysis considering market, technical, financial, and 
environmental factors.
co3_text:
Prepare cost estimates, financial plans, and funding structures for 
agribusiness projects.
co4_text:
Evaluate projects using financial appraisal techniques and risk assessment 
tools.
co5_text:
Monitor and assess project implementation through scheduling, 
performance indicators, and post-evaluation methods.
unit1_text:
Unit 1: Introduction to Project Finance (9 Hours) 
Overview of project finance in agribusiness; Importance and role of project finance in agricultural 
development; Types of agribusiness projects: production, processing, infrastructure; Project life cycle 
and stages; Sources of project finance: equity, debt, grants, subsidies; Role of financial institutions 
and government schemes in agribusiness project financing
unit2_text:
Unit 2: Project Identification and Feasibility Analysis (9 Hours) 
Project identification and screening; Market analysis for agribusiness projects; Technical feasibility: 
location, technology, capacity planning; Financial feasibility: cost estimates, revenue projections; 
Economic feasibility and social considerations; Environmental impact assessment; Case studies on 
project feasibility in various agribusiness sectors
unit3_text:
Unit 3: Project Costing and Financial Planning (10 Hours) 
Estimation of project costs: fixed and variable costs; Working capital requirements and management; 
Preparation of project financial statements: projected income statement, balance sheet, cash flow 
statement; Sources of funds and capital structure for projects; Financial planning and budgeting for 
agribusiness projects; Case examples of project cost structuring
unit4_text:
Unit 4: Project Appraisal Techniques (10 Hours) 
Concept and objectives of project appraisal; Financial appraisal techniques: Payback Period, Net 
Present Value (NPV), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR), Profitability Index; 
Sensitivity analysis and risk assessment in project appraisal; Break-even analysis and cash flow risk 
evaluation; Social cost-benefit analysis and project sustainability; Case studies illustrating project 
appraisal in agribusiness
unit5_text:
Unit 5: Project Implementation, Monitoring, and Evaluation (10 Hours) 
Project implementation process and challenges; Earned Value Analysis (EVA); Monitoring project 
progress and performance indicators; Post-implementation review and project evaluation; Role of 
audit and feedback mechanisms; Managing project risks and mitigation strategies; Examples of 
successful and failed agribusiness projects with lessons learned

co1_text: Describe the nature, scope, and decision areas in farm business management.
co2_text: Apply economic principles such as equi-marginal returns and opportunity cost in solving farm-level problems.
co3_text: Develop and interpret farm plans, budgets, and net worth statements for business decision-making.

unit1_text:
UNIT I: Introduction to Farm Business Management (5 hours)
Nature, scope, and characteristics of farm business management; Role and functions of farm business
management in agribusiness; Types of farm management decisions and their significance;
Identification and analysis of farm management problems
unit2_text:
UNIT II: Principles of Farm Management Decisions (10 hours)
Principle of variable proportion in resource allocation; Cost principles in farm decision making;
Principle of factor substitution; Law of equi-marginal returns and its applications; Opportunity cost
principle and its relevance; Other relevant decision-making principles in farm management
unit3_text:
UNIT III: Tools of Farm Management and Business Analysis (9 hours)
Farm planning: concepts and process; Farm budgeting: types (partial, complete), steps, and sample
budgets; Farm records and accounts: types, significance, common problems; Preparation and
interpretation of net worth statements; Farm efficiency measures: productivity and profitability
analysis
unit4_text:
UNIT IV: Management of Farm Resources (8 hours)
Land resource management: land use efficiency, optimal allocation; Management of agricultural
labor: deployment, wages, and productivity; Farm machinery management: selection, investment, and
operations; Farm buildings and infrastructure: planning and maintenance
unit5_text:
UNIT V: Risk and Uncertainty in Farming (8 hours)
Sources and types of risk and uncertainty in farm business; Risk management strategies:
diversification, insurance, hedging, etc.; Decision-making under risk and uncertainty: approaches and
models; Practical cases illustrating risk, uncertainty, and risk mitigation in farm business management

unit1_text:
Unit I: Cooperative Administration — A Global Perspective (8 Hours) 
Overview of cooperative administration worldwide; Ecology of cooperative administration: 
environment and factors influencing cooperatives; Role of the cooperative sector in economic 
development and rural empowerment
unit2_text:
Unit II: Cooperative Management — Nature and Functions (8 Hours) 
Nature, functions, and objectives of cooperative organizations; Key activities: procurement, storage, 
processing, and marketing in cooperatives; Process of cooperative formation and development stages; 
Importance of leadership and governance in cooperative management
unit3_text:
Unit III: Government Role and Cooperative Policy (10 Hours) 
Role of the state in promoting and regulating cooperatives; Effects of cooperative laws on 
management and operations; Long-range planning and strategies for cooperative expansion; Policy 
formulation and implementation for cooperative development
unit4_text:
Unit IV: Human Resource and Board Management in Cooperatives (7 Hours) 
Human resource management practices in cooperative organizations; Recruitment, placement, and 
development of cooperative staff; Roles, responsibilities, and functioning of the board of directors; 
Decision-making and accountability in cooperative governance
unit5_text:
Unit V: Agribusiness Cooperatives — Types and Financing (7 Hours) 
Overview of different types of agribusiness cooperatives: credit cooperatives, marketing cooperatives, 
dairy cooperatives; Financing mechanisms and sources for agribusiness cooperatives; Challenges and 
opportunities in cooperative financing and sustainability

unit1_text:
Unit I: Introduction to Bank Credit Management (8 Hrs.)
Credit Risk Management: Meaning and significance, Lending policies and procedures, Types of credit
facilities: funded and non-funded facilities, Steps in lending process, Credit information and role of credit
information Bureau; and management of credit portfolio. Principles and regulation of lending; credit policies
and procedures; credit manuals; organization of credit function; and credit committee.
unit2_text:
Unit 2: Credit Evaluation Process (8 Hrs.)
Credit scoring; credit rating; financial analysis; ratios analysis: profitability ratios, liquidity ratios and
measures, measuring efficiency, financial leverage, review of financial indicators; common size statement
analysis.
unit3_text:
Unit 3: Commercial and industrial lending (8 Hrs.)
Role of asymmetric information in lending; the competitive environment; loan policy; making loan; principal
lending activities; collateral: characteristics of goods collateral, types of collateral; the lending process:
evaluating a loan request, structuring commercial loan agreements, pricing commercial loan, and monitoring
and loan reviews. On-Fund Based Operations :  Bank guarantees; letter of credit: meaning and types,
establishing letter of credit, parties involved, basic documents, risk assessment in letter of credit
unit4_text:
Unit 4 Real Estates and Consumer Lending (8 Hrs.)
Real Estate lending: mortgage debt outstanding, characteristics of mortgage loan, the real estate portfolio,
residential mortgage loan, alternative space mortgage instruments, technology, commercial real estate loan;
consumer lending: types of consumer loan, leases, finance charges, annual percentage rate, real estate and
consumer credit regulation.
unit5_text:
Unit 5: Credit Administration, Monitoring and Review (8 Hrs.)
Credit structuring; bank documentation; types of securities and methods of creating charge over securities;
loan covenants; credit file and credit evaluation memo; sanction and disbursement; follow up mechanism for
monitoring; indicators of problem loans; credit audit; Handling problem loans: Credit restructuring: non-
performing assets and Provisioning norms; non-banking assets. Characteristics of credit risk, indicators of
credit risk, credit risk and bank failure, mitigating credit risk

unit1_text:
Module I: Fundamental Concepts (6 Hours) 
Introduction: Definition; Cannons of Taxation; Person; Assessee; Income; Previous Year; Assessment Year; Income Tax; Important Dates and Forms. Residential Status & Tax Incidence: Individual; Income Exempted from Tax.
unit2_text:
Module II Heads of Income and Provisions (10 Hours) 
Heads of Income: Salaries; Income from House Property; Profits & Gains from Business or Profession; Capital Gains; Income from Other Sources. Clubbing of Incomes; Calculation of Taxable Income; Tax Calculation including Surcharge and Marginal Relief; Deduction; Rebate; Relief; Set-off & Carry Forward of Losses – Principles; Meaning; Inter-source & Inter-head Set-off.
unit3_text:
Module III: Tax Planning & Management (8 Hours) 
Tax Avoidance; Tax Planning; Tax Evasion. Income Tax Authorities: Their Appointment; Jurisdiction; Powers and Functions. Tax Administration: Provisions relating to Collection and Recovery of Tax; Refund of Tax; Offences; Penalties and Prosecutions; Appeals and Revisions; Advance Tax; Tax Deducted at Source (TDS); Advance Rulings; Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreements (DTAA).
unit4_text:
Module IV: Corporate Tax (6 Hours) 
Computation of Taxable Income; Carry-forward and Set-off of Losses for Companies; Minimum Alternative Tax (MAT); Set-off and Carry-forward of Amalgamation Losses; Tax Planning for Amalgamation, Merger and Demerger of Companies; Tax Provisions for Venture Capital Funds.

unit1_text:
Module I: Monetary Policy and Macroeconomic Environment Management (6 Hours) 
Monetary Policy and Macroeconomic Environment Management; Concept and Importance of Monetary Policy; 
Objectives of Monetary Policy: Price Stability, Employment Generation, Exchange Rate Stability, Balanced Economic 
Growth and Financial Stability. Conflict among Monetary Policy Objectives: Growth versus Inflation; Role of Monetary 
Policy in Economic Development; Inflation Management; Monetary Policy Transmission Mechanism; Role of Central 
Bank in Macroeconomic Management. Case Studies: Monetary policy responses during inflationary pressures and 
economic slowdown.
unit2_text:
Module II: RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee and Monetary Policy Instruments (10 Hours) 
Formation of Monetary Policy Committee (MPC): Purpose, Functions, Constitution and Decision-Making Process; 
Instruments of Monetary Policy: Concept, Mechanism and Effectiveness of: Bank Rate, Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), 
Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR), Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) Rate; Review of 
Monetary Policy Framework of the Reserve Bank of India during the last five years; Recent Monetary Policy Changes 
announced by RBI. Role of Central Banking in Emerging Economies; Digital Currency and Changing Role of Central 
Banks. Case Studies: RBI monetary policy decisions and their impact on inflation, growth and financial markets.
unit3_text:
Module III: Public Finance and Recent Macroeconomic Trends (8 Hours) 
Public Finance: Meaning, Scope and Importance; Role of Government in the Economy. Government Intervention: 
Public Goods, Externalities and Asymmetric Information. Fiscal Policy and Long-Term Economic Growth; Fiscal Policy 
and Equity; Fiscal Policy and Macroeconomic Stability. Interaction between Monetary Policy and Fiscal Policy; Fiscal-
Monetary Coordination. Recent Global and Regional Macroeconomic Trends; Impact of Global Economic Events on 
Domestic Policy Framework. Case Studies: Global financial crises, pandemic response, and economic recovery policies.
unit4_text:
Module IV: Fiscal Frameworks, Policies and Economic Impact (10 Hours) 
Fiscal Policy: Meaning, Objectives and Components. Government Expenditure in India: Capital Expenditure, Revenue 
Expenditure, Plan and Non-Plan Expenditure Fiscal Indicators: Fiscal Deficit, Primary Deficit,  Revenue Deficit; Impact 
of Fiscal Deficits on Economic Growth and Stability; Government Receipts: Capital Receipts, Revenue Receipts, Tax 
Revenue Non-Tax Revenue; Budget Estimates, Revised Estimates and Actual Estimates; Modern Budgeting Practices: 
Zero-Based Budgeting, Gender Budgeting; Fiscal Devolution and Centre-State Financial Relations; Role of Finance 
Commission; Case Studies: Union Budget analysis and fiscal policy reforms in India.
unit5_text:
Module V: Fiscal Policy Sustainability and Inclusive Growth (6 Hours) 
Fiscal Sustainability: Concept and Importance; Public Debt Management; Debt Tolerance and Fiscal Space. 
Fiscal Sustainability Analysis: Debt Projections,  Fiscal Risks,  Debt Sustainability Across Countries and Over Time 
Fiscal Space: Concept, Optimal and Safe Debt Levels; Relationship between Interest Rates and Public Debt. 
Fiscal Policy and Inclusive Growth: Poverty Reduction,  Employment Generation, Social Sector Development 
Sustainable Economic Growth; Case Studies: Sustainable fiscal practices and inclusive development strategies.

unit1_text:
Module I: Introduction to Treasury Management (8 Hours)
Overview of Treasury Management; Meaning, Concept and Importance of Treasury Management in Banking; Role of
Treasury in Financial Institutions; Impact of Treasury Operations on Bank Profitability; Functions and Responsibilities
of Treasury Department in Banks; Structure and Organization of Bank Treasury; Front Office, Middle Office and Back
Office Functions; Regulatory Framework for Treasury Operations; Risk Management in Treasury Operations.
unit2_text:
Module II: Money Markets and Fixed Income Securities (8 Hours)
Concept and Structure of Money Market; Money Market Instruments; Treasury Bills; Commercial Papers; Certificates
of Deposit; Call Money Market; Repurchase Agreements (Repo); Fixed Income Securities; Bonds; Government
Securities; Corporate Bonds; Features and Classification of Fixed Income Instruments; Yield Curves; Bond Pricing;
Valuation of Fixed Income Securities; Yield Measurement and Interest Rate Sensitivity.
unit3_text:
Module III: Foreign Exchange Management (8 Hours)
Overview of Foreign Exchange Markets; Participants in Foreign Exchange Markets; Foreign Exchange Operations in
Banks; Exchange Rate Mechanism; Foreign Exchange Risk Management; Types of Foreign Exchange Exposure; Hedging
Techniques; Currency Derivatives; Forward Contracts; Futures Contracts; Options; Swaps; Managing Exchange Rate
Fluctuations in International Trade; Role of Treasury in Forex Management.
unit4_text:
Module IV: Liquidity and Cash Management (8 Hours)
Liquidity Management in Banking and Financial Institutions; Importance of Liquidity Management; Cash Flow
Forecasting; Working Capital Management; Cash Position Management; Cash Pooling; Cash Concentration; Cash
Positioning Strategies; Liquidity Planning and Optimization; Asset Liability Management (ALM); Liquidity Risk
Management.
unit5_text:
Module V: Risk Management and Compliance in Treasury Operations (8 Hours)
Financial Risks in Treasury Operations; Identification and Measurement of Risks; Interest Rate Risk; Credit Risk; Market
Risk; Operational Risk; Risk Measurement Techniques; Value at Risk (VaR); Basel III Framework and its Impact on
Treasury Risk Management; Regulatory Compliance; Internal Controls; Treasury Audit; Reporting Requirements;
Corporate Governance in Treasury Operations.

Role of Risk Management in Economic Growth and Business Sustainability; Risk Management Functions; Role and 
Responsibilities of Risk Manager; Risk Management Process; Risk Identification; Risk Assessment and Evaluation; Risk 
Response Strategies; Risk Control and Risk Financing; Risk Management Plan Administration; Risk Management in 
Global Economy; Future Perspectives of Risk Management.

Insurance Contract: Meaning, Nature and Importance; Subject Matter of Insurance; Principles of Insurance Contract;

and Documentation; Evidence and Supporting Documents; Payment of Premium; Policy Issuance Process; E-Insurance 
Policy; Insurance Repositories; Digital Transformation in Insurance Services.
